whatGodIsSaying.headline: Underneath Are the Everlasting Arms: The Departure of the Friend of God
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Deuteronomy 34 is one of the most tender, majestic scenes in all of literature. Moses is 120 years old. He has led this stiff-necked nation for forty years through desert sands, mutinies, and miracles. And now, God calls him to climb Mount Nebo alone. Look at verse 7: 'His eye was not dim, nor his natural vigor diminished.' Moses did not die of sickness, senility, or disease. He climbed that rugged mountain on his own two feet, standing at the summit of Pisgah with God.

Look at what God did for His friend. God stood beside Moses and personally gave him a supernatural panoramic view of the Promised Land—from the snow-capped peak of Mount Hermon in Dan to the blue waters of the Mediterranean, down to the palm trees of Jericho. God showed him the fulfillment of the covenant sworn to Abraham six centuries earlier.

And then, look at verse 5-6: 'So Moses the servant of Yahweh died there... according to the word of Yahweh. And He buried him in the valley... but no man knows where his tomb is to this day.' The Hebrew phrase 'according to the word of Yahweh' literally translates as *al-pi Yahweh*—'at the mouth of Yahweh.' Ancient Jewish commentators reverently described it as Moses dying **by the kiss of God**! The Creator of the universe gently closed the eyes of His faithful servant, and God Himself dug his grave and laid him to rest. Why did God hide the grave? Because if fallen humanity knew where Moses was buried, they would have turned his tomb into an idolatrous shrine! God kept Moses' resting place secret, preserving the purity of worship.

And notice the final words of Deuteronomy: 'There has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom Yahweh knew face to face.' Moses was great, but Deuteronomy ends with a question mark, looking for the ultimate Prophet like Moses whom God promised in Deuteronomy 18:15. Fifteen centuries later, on the Mount of Transfiguration (Matthew 17), Moses finally stepped foot inside the Promised Land! He stood on the holy mountain talking with Jesus Christ—the true and greater Prophet—speaking of the ultimate Exodus Jesus was about to accomplish on the cross! Your earthly finish line is not the end of your story; underneath your life are the everlasting arms.

lessons.lesson: Rest Confidently in God's Everlasting Arms
lessons.detail: Moses sang: 'The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms.' No matter how far you fall or how turbulent life becomes, God's eternal arms are beneath you to catch and sustain you.

lessons.lesson: Intimacy with God Is the Supreme Measurement of a Life
lessons.detail: Moses' ultimate epitaph was not his miracles, plagues, or laws, but that 'Yahweh knew him face to face.' At the end of your days, the only statistic that matters is how deeply you walked with God.

profile.title: Joshua: The Successor Stepping into the River
profile.who: Joshua (Hoshea, 'Yahweh is salvation'), son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, longtime faithful assistant to Moses, general of the army, and faithful spy, commissioned directly by Yahweh to lead Israel across the Jordan to conquer Canaan.

profile.family: Joshua son of Nun; tribe of Ephraim; spiritual son and successor to Moses.
keyMoments: Following the thirty days of mourning for Moses, Yahweh spoke directly to Joshua: 'Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, you, and all this people, into the land which I give to them.'
God gave the colossal territorial promise: 'Every place that the sole of your foot will tread on, I have given to you... from the wilderness and Lebanon to the great river Euphrates.'
God gave the supreme personal assurance: 'As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you, nor forsake you.'
Three times God commanded: 'Be strong and of a good courage... be strong and very courageous... Don't be afraid, neither be dismayed: for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.'

God gave the key to biblical leadership: 'This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night... for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.'
Joshua commanded the officers to prepare provisions: within three days they would cross the Jordan.
Addressed the two-and-a-half tribes (Reuben, Gad, half-Manasseh), reminding them of their pledge to cross armed ahead of their brothers to fight until all rested.
Israel answered with complete allegiance: 'All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go... only Yahweh your God be with you, as he was with Moses!'
Joshua secretly dispatched two spies from Shittim to explore Jericho and the surrounding territory.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Arise and Cross Over: The Mandate of Courage and the Word
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Imagine the crushing weight that fell upon Joshua's shoulders in Joshua 1:2. The chapter opens with four devastating words: 'Moses My servant is dead.' For forty years, Moses had been the spiritual giant, the lawgiver, the father of the nation, the friend of God. Moses was all Joshua had ever known. Now Moses was gone, and God looked at Joshua and said: 'Now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, you and all this people!' How do you step into the shoes of Moses?

Notice how God equipped Joshua. God did not give him advanced chariot blueprints, siege engines, or secret military tactics. God gave him two things: **His presence** and **His Word**! In verse 5, God promised: 'As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.' And three times God commanded him: 'Be strong and courageous!' (vv. 6, 7, 9). Notice why Joshua could be courageous: not because Joshua was a military genius, but because 'Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go!' Real courage is not the absence of fear; it is the presence of God conquering our fear.

And look at the secret to biblical success in verse 8: 'This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night... for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success!' The Hebrew word for 'meditate' is *hagah*—to mutter, chew, speak, and digest God's Word constantly. God told this military general: 'Your victory will not be won by your sword, but by your saturation in My Word!' When your mind is anchored in Scripture and your feet walk in obedience, God Himself guarantees your success.

lessons.lesson: Courage Is Rooted in the Guarantee of God's Presence
lessons.detail: God told Joshua: 'Don't be afraid... for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.' We can face terrifying assignments and massive life transitions with bold courage because God never leaves our side.

profile.title: Rahab: The Scarlet Cord in the Wall of Jericho
profile.who: Rahab, an innkeeper and prostitute in the doomed pagan city of Jericho, whose keen spiritual discernment recognized Yahweh as the supreme God of heaven and earth, risking her life to hide the Hebrew spies and securing salvation for her entire household.
profile.whenAndWhere: The city walls of Jericho in the Jordan Valley, around 1406 BC.
profile.family: Canaanite prostitute; father, mother, brothers, sisters, and extended household.
keyMoments: Two Hebrew spies sent by Joshua arrived secretly in Jericho and lodged in Rahab's house, which was built into the outer city wall.
The king of Jericho learned of their presence and sent soldiers commanding Rahab to surrender the men.
Rahab hid the spies under stalks of flax drying on her flat roof, sending the king's pursuers on a wild goose chase toward the Jordan fords.

Went up to the roof before the spies slept and delivered one of the most stunning theological confessions of faith in the Old Testament: 'I know that Yahweh has given you the land... for we have heard how Yahweh dried up the water of the Red Sea... for Yahweh your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath!'
Extracted a solemn oath of covenant mercy: because she showed kindness to them, they must spare her life, her father, mother, brothers, and sisters when Jericho fell.

The spies agreed on three conditions: 1) she must not betray their business; 2) her entire family must stay inside her house; 3) she must bind a specific **scarlet cord** in the window through which she let them down.
Let them down by a rope through her window outside the city wall and advised them to hide in the limestone mountains three days until pursuers returned.
Immediately tied the scarlet cord in her window, a beacon of redemption in the doomed wall.

When Jericho's walls collapsed, Rahab's house stood intact; Joshua sent the two spies to bring her and her family out safely; she was welcomed into Israel, married Salmon of the tribe of Judah, became the mother of Boaz, and entered the royal genealogy of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:5).
strengths: Profound spiritual perception: recognized that Yahweh is the true God of heaven and earth while all Jericho trembled in blind denial.
Courageous faith: risked execution for high treason to align herself with the people of God.
Fierce love for her family: insisted that her parents, brothers, and sisters be included in the covenant of rescue.
failures: Lived in deep moral compromise as a pagan Canaanite prostitute before encountering the truth of Yahweh.
Spoke a deceptive misdirection to the king's soldiers, reflecting the imperfect ethics of her pagan background, yet praised by Scripture exclusively for her saving faith.

scripture.title: Rahab Hides the Spies, Confesses Yahweh, and the Scarlet Cord Oath

verses.text: Joshua the son of Nun secretly sent two men out of Shittim as spies, saying, 'Go, view the land, including Jericho.' They went and came into the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahab, and slept there.
The woman took the two men, and hid them. Then she said, 'Yes, the men came to me, but I didn’t know where they came from.'
She said to the men, 'I know that Yahweh has given you the land, and that the fear of you has fallen on us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.'
'As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted, neither did there remain any more spirit in any man, because of you: for Yahweh your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.'
'Now therefore, please swear to me by Yahweh, since I have dealt kindly with you, that you also will deal kindly with my father’s house, and give me a true token;'
'and that you will save alive my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters, and all that they have, and will deliver our lives from death.'
Then she let them down by a cord through the window; for her house was on the side of the wall, and she lived on the wall.

'Behold, when we come into the land, you shall bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to let us down... and gather to yourself into the house your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father’s household.'
She said, 'According to your words, so be it.' She sent them away, and they departed. She tied the scarlet line in the window.

scripture.title: By Faith: The Walls of Jericho and Rahab's Salvation

verses.text: By faith, the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been encircled for seven days.
By faith, Rahab the prostitute didn’t perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies in peace.
What more shall I say? For the time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets;
who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked out righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
These all, having had testimony given to them through their faith, didn’t receive the promise,
God having provided some better thing concerning us, that apart from us they should not be made perfect.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: The Scarlet Cord in the Window: Grace for the Outcast
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Rahab is one of the most stunning trophies of divine grace in all of world literature. Look at her background: She was a **Canaanite**—a member of a corrupt, pagan culture under divine judgment. And she was a **prostitute**—a woman whose life was marked by brokenness, shame, and social stigma. If ancient religious legalists were drawing up a list of candidates for God's mercy, Rahab would have been at the absolute bottom.

Yet look at her faith! In Joshua 2:11, this pagan woman spoke words of theological brilliance that outshone the ten unbelieving Hebrew spies at Kadesh: 'For Yahweh your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath!' While the mighty king of Jericho and his warriors were paralyzed in terror, Rahab made a decisive, courageous choice: she renounced her doomed city and threw herself on the mercy of the living God!

And look at the token of her salvation: **a scarlet cord tied in her window!** Just as the blood of the Passover lamb on the doorposts marked Hebrew homes for salvation in Egypt, that crimson cord dangling from the wall of Jericho marked Rahab's house for salvation in Canaan! When the trumpets blasted and the megalithic stone walls of Jericho came crashing down in rubble, one section of the wall remained standing like a solitary tower of mercy: the house with the scarlet cord!

Even more breathtaking is what God did with Rahab's future. God did not relegate her to second-class status. She was welcomed into the covenant community of Israel, married Salmon (a prince of Judah), gave birth to godly Boaz, became the great-great-grandmother of King David, and is named in Matthew 1:5 in the royal genealogy of Jesus Christ! James 2:25 celebrates her works of faith, and Hebrews 11:31 enshrines her in the Hall of Faith. No matter how broken, messy, or stained your past may be, the scarlet blood of Christ can redeem your life and write you into God's royal family!

lessons.lesson: No Past Is Too Broken for God's Transforming Grace
lessons.detail: Rahab was a Canaanite prostitute, yet by faith she was redeemed, honored in Scripture, and grafted into the genealogy of the Messiah. Your past does not define your future when surrendered to God.
lessons.question: Is there past shame, failure, or brokenness in your life that you need to surrender to the redemptive blood of Christ?

lessons.lesson: True Faith Takes Action Even at Great Personal Cost
lessons.detail: Rahab did not merely admire God from afar; she risked her life to hide the spies and align with God's people. Genuine faith always expresses itself in concrete, courageous action.
lessons.question: Does your faith manifest in tangible, courageous choices, or does it remain merely intellectual belief?

lessons.lesson: The Scarlet Cord Points to the Cross of Christ
lessons.detail: The scarlet cord in Rahab's window shielded everyone inside her house from Jericho's collapse. The shed blood of Jesus Christ is our only shelter when worldly systems crumble in judgment.
lessons.question: Is your life and household securely gathered under the protective shelter of the blood of Jesus?

lessons.lesson: Bring Your Entire Family Under the Umbrella of Faith
lessons.detail: Rahab did not seek salvation for herself alone; she pleaded fiercely for her parents, brothers, and sisters. Intercede passionately for your loved ones, inviting them into the safety of God's covenant.
lessons.question: Which family members are you actively praying for, asking God to bring them into the safety of His salvation?

quiz.question: What profession and nationality did Rahab have when the spies arrived in Jericho in Joshua 2:1?
quiz.explanation: Scripture explicitly records that she was a Canaanite prostitute in Jericho whose name was Rahab.

quiz.question: Where did Rahab hide the two Hebrew spies when the king's soldiers searched her house in Joshua 2:6?
options: In a dry cistern in the courtyard
Under the stalks of flax which she had laid in order on the roof
quiz.explanation: She brought them up to the roof and hid them with the stalks of flax which she had spread out.

quiz.question: What confession of faith did Rahab make to the spies in Joshua 2:11?
options: 'The gods of Canaan are strong, but Yahweh is richer'
'Yahweh your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath'
'I want to buy silver from Israel'
quiz.explanation: Rahab boldly confessed: '...for Yahweh your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.'

quiz.question: What sign was Rahab instructed to bind in her window to mark her house for salvation in Joshua 2:18?
quiz.explanation: The spies commanded her: '...you shall bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to let us down...'

quiz.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 11:31, Rahab the prostitute is included in the Hall of Faith because by faith she didn't perish with the disobedient.
quiz.explanation: True. Hebrews 11:31 honors her: 'By faith, Rahab the prostitute didn’t perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies in peace.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of heaven above and earth beneath, Your mercy is an ocean that washes away the deepest stains of human brokenness! Thank You for the story of Rahab, which proves that no background is too compromised, no life too sinful, and no past too dark for Your redeeming love. Thank You for the scarlet cord of Jesus Christ's blood, which marks my soul for salvation while the judgments of this fallen world fall around me. Deliver me from self-righteous judgment of others; give me the eyes of grace to see the potential for redemption in the outcasts and broken around me. Bring my entire family into the safety of Your covenant house, and let my life be a monument of Your scandalous, life-saving grace. In Jesus' name, Amen.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Lord, by faith I tie the scarlet cord of Christ's blood over my life and household, trusting in Your great salvation.
closingPrayer.prompt: Thank Jesus for His redeeming blood that washes away your past, and pray for someone you know who feels 'too broken' for God to save.

73.season: Crossing the Jordan on Dry Ground
73.theme: When we step into the floodwaters in obedience, God halts the raging currents and carves a dry path of triumph.

memoryVerse.text: That all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of Yahweh, that it is mighty, and that you may fear Yahweh your God forever.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: The twelve memorial stones from the dry bed of the Jordan stand as a perpetual reminder that God's mighty hand makes a way through floodwaters so that all nations may know His power.

cramData.firstLetters: T a t p o t e m k t h o Y, t i i m, a t y m f Y y G f.

profile.title: Joshua & Israel: The Parted Flood and the Twelve Memorial Stones
profile.who: Joshua, commanding over two million Israelites to sanctify themselves as the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant stepped into the flood-stage waters of the Jordan River, witnessing the river stand in a heap thirty miles upstream.
profile.whenAndWhere: The Jordan River crossing opposite Jericho, tenth day of the first month, around 1406 BC.
profile.family: Joshua, High Priest Eleazar, the twelve tribal representatives carrying stones, all Israel.
keyMoments: Israel broke camp at Shittim and lodged at the Jordan River; the river was in full spring flood stage, overflowing all its banks during the barley harvest.
Joshua commanded the people: 'Sanctify yourselves! For tomorrow Yahweh will do wonders among you.'
Instructed the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant to march ahead of the people, keeping a reverent distance of two thousand cubits (half a mile).
God told Joshua: 'Today I will begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.'

The priests marched forward; the moment the soles of their feet touched the brink of the overflowing water, the waters coming down from upstream stopped and rose up in a heap at the city of Adam, thirty miles away!
The waters flowing down toward the Salt Sea were completely cut off; the priests stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the riverbed while all Israel crossed over on dry ground.
Joshua commanded twelve chosen men—one from each tribe—to take twelve large stones from the middle of the Jordan where the priests stood, and build a memorial cairn at Gilgal.
Joshua also erected twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan Riverbed where the priests' feet stood.
When the priests came up out of the riverbed and the soles of their feet touched dry land, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and overflowed all its banks as before.

Israel camped at Gilgal on the tenth day of the first month—the exact day Passover lambs were selected—and Joshua explained the stones: 'When your children ask in time to come, "What mean these stones?" tell them: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land!'
strengths: Faith of the priests: stepped into rushing floodwaters before the river parted.
Joshua prioritized spiritual consecration before military action ('Sanctify yourselves').
Built intentional memorial monuments to pass down faith to future generations.
failures: Scripture records no failure here; Israel crossed in triumphant, disciplined obedience.

scripture.title: Sanctification, the Priests' Feet in the Brink, and the Jordan Parted

verses.text: Joshua said to the people, 'Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow Yahweh will do wonders among you.'
Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Today I will begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.'

'It shall happen, when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of Yahweh, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off, even the waters that come down from above; and they shall stand in one heap.'

and when those who bore the ark had come to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who bore the ark were dipped in the edge of the water (for the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest),

that the waters which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap, a great deal off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. Then the people passed over opposite Jericho.

The priests who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan; and all Israel passed over on dry ground, until all the nation had passed completely over the Jordan.

scripture.title: Twelve Stones from the Riverbed, Gilgal Camp, and the Witness to Nations

verses.text: 'Take twelve men out of the people, out of every tribe a man,'

'and command them, saying, "Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, and carry them over with you, and lay them down in the place where you’ll lodge tonight."'
Joshua set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood; and they are there to this day.

When the priests who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant had come up out of the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet were lifted up to the dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place, and overflowed all its banks, as before.
Joshua set up those twelve stones, which they took out of the Jordan, in Gilgal.
He spoke to the children of Israel, saying, 'When your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, "What do these stones mean?"'
'Then you shall let your children know, saying, "Israel came over this Jordan on dry land."'
'that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of Yahweh, that it is mighty, and that you may fear Yahweh your God forever.'

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Wet Feet Before Dry Ground: Stepping into the Impossible
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Look at the timing of the Jordan crossing in Joshua 3:15: 'The Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest.' God did not lead Israel to the Jordan during the dry summer months when the river was a sluggish, knee-deep stream. God brought them to the riverbank during the spring harvest runoff, when melting snow from Mount Hermon turned the Jordan into a raging, torrential, muddy brown flood over a mile wide! To human eyes, crossing was suicidal.

Now notice the divine requirement in verse 13: God told the priests carrying the heavy Ark of the Covenant: 'When the soles of your feet rest in the waters, the waters shall be cut off.' Notice the order: **God did not part the waters while the priests were sitting comfortably in their tents!** The priests had to march forward, carry the Ark on their shoulders, and step directly into the roaring floodwater! It was only when their sandals got wet—only when they stepped into the edge of the river in radical obedience—that the roaring current halted thirty miles upstream at the city of Adam!

Faith is not waiting until all problems vanish before you obey. Faith is stepping forward in obedience while the river is still flooding, knowing that the God who commands you will hold back the waters. And look at what Joshua did in Joshua 4: he took twelve heavy stones from the dry riverbed and built an altar at Gilgal. Why? Because human beings are chronically prone to forgetfulness! When life is hard, we forget God's past miracles. Joshua said: 'When your children ask in time to come, "What mean these stones?" tell them: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land!' Build memorial stones of thanksgiving in your heart so your faith never forgets God's mighty hand.

lessons.lesson: Faith Steps into the Water Before the Miracle Happens
lessons.detail: The waters did not part until the priests dipped their feet into the overflowing current. God often waits for us to take the first step of obedient faith before He supernaturally removes the obstacle.
lessons.question: What step of obedience is God asking you to take right now that requires you to 'get your feet wet' before seeing the outcome?

lessons.lesson: Consecration Must Always Precede Divine Breakthrough
lessons.detail: Joshua commanded: 'Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow Yahweh will do wonders among you.' When you desire God's supernatural power and breakthrough, begin by purifying your heart and setting yourself apart for Him.
lessons.question: Are you asking God for outward wonders and breakthroughs while neglecting inward holiness and consecration?

lessons.lesson: Build Memorial Stones to Remember God's Faithfulness
lessons.detail: The twelve stones at Gilgal stood as an enduring teaching tool for future generations. Keep a journal, celebrate anniversaries of answered prayer, and recount God's past deliverances to your children.
lessons.question: What 'memorial stones' of past deliverances can you share with your family or friends this week to strengthen their faith?

lessons.lesson: God's Wonders Reveal His Mighty Hand to the Entire World
lessons.detail: The Jordan was parted so that 'all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of Yahweh, that it is mighty.' God's miracles in your life are designed to testify of His saving power to a watching world.
lessons.question: How can your testimony of God making a way through impossible circumstances point non-believers to Jesus?

quiz.question: What condition was the Jordan River in when Israel crossed over in Joshua 3:15?
options: It was completely dry from a severe drought
It was frozen solid with winter ice
It overflowed all its banks during harvest time
It had been diverted by Canaanite dams
quiz.explanation: Scripture explicitly notes parenthetically: '...for the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest...'

quiz.question: At what moment did the waters of the Jordan stop flowing and rise up in a heap in Joshua 3:15-16?
options: When Joshua struck the water with Moses' rod
When the feet of the priests who bore the ark were dipped in the edge of the water
After Israel fasted for three days
At midnight when the trumpet sounded
quiz.explanation: The waters rose up in a heap the moment the feet of the priests bearing the ark were dipped in the edge of the water.

quiz.question: Where did the waters rising upstream stand in a heap according to Joshua 3:16?
options: At the city of Adam, beside Zarethan
quiz.explanation: The waters stood and rose up in one heap a great deal off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan.

quiz.question: How many stones were taken from the middle of the riverbed to build the memorial at Gilgal in Joshua 4:2-3?
quiz.explanation: Twelve men, one out of each tribe, took twelve stones from where the priests stood firm in the riverbed.

quiz.question: True or False: According to Joshua 4:24, the purpose of the Jordan memorial stones was that all peoples of the earth may know the hand of Yahweh, that it is mighty, and that Israel may fear Yahweh forever.
quiz.explanation: True. Joshua 4:24 explicitly gives this worldwide missional purpose.

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of the impossible, You are the Lord of all the earth! Before Your Ark and Your holy presence, raging floodwaters stop and rise up in a heap. Forgive me for the hesitation and fear that keeps me standing on the riverbank, waiting for circumstances to part before I obey. Give me the faith of the priests to step boldly into the edge of the water, trusting Your Word. Consecrate my heart today, Lord; cleanse me of all compromise, for You desire to do wonders in and through my life. Thank You for the memorial stones of Your past deliverances in my life. Let Your mighty hand be revealed through my testimony, that all the peoples of the earth may know that You are God and fear Your holy Name forever. In Jesus' name, Amen.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Lord, let all the peoples of the earth know that Your hand is mighty, as I step forward in faith through every flood.
closingPrayer.prompt: Identify an area where you have been waiting for God to move before you obey, and take that first step of faith today.

74.season: The Commander of the Lord's Army and Jericho's Walls
74.theme: Spiritual victory is not won by getting God on our side, but by surrendering unconditionally to the Commander of the Lord's army.

memoryVerse.text: He said, 'No; but I have come now as commander of Yahweh’s army.' Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and worshiped, and said to him, 'What does my lord say to his servant?'
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: God does not enlist in human causes; He takes command. When we fall on our faces in surrender before King Jesus, fortified walls of impossibility collapse before Him.

cramData.firstLetters: H s, 'N; b I h c n a c o Y a.' J f o h f t t e, a w, a s t h, 'W d m l s t h s?'

profile.title: Joshua: The Swordsman at the Feet of the Commander
profile.who: Joshua, reconnoitering the colossal fortifications of Jericho, confronted by the pre-incarnate Christ as the Commander of Yahweh's army with drawn sword, receiving the unconventional battle plan of silent marches and trumpet blasts that flattened Jericho's walls.
profile.whenAndWhere: The plains before the fortified city of Jericho, around 1406 BC.
profile.family: Joshua, Priests carrying the Ark and seven shofars, armed men of Israel.
keyMoments: At Gilgal, the new generation was circumcised, rolling away the reproach of Egypt; celebrated Passover; the manna ceased, and they ate the produce of Canaan.
Joshua walked near Jericho assessing its impregnable walls; looked up and saw a Man standing opposite him with a drawn sword in His hand.
Joshua boldly approached: 'Are you for us, or for our adversaries?'
The heavenly Figure replied with the shocking word: 'No; but I have come now as commander of Yahweh’s army!'
Joshua instantly fell on his face to the earth, worshiped, and asked: 'What does my lord say to his servant?'
The Commander said: 'Take off your sandals from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy.' Joshua did so.
God delivered the bizarre divine battle strategy: march around the city once a day for six days with the Ark and seven priests blowing rams' horns, all soldiers maintaining complete silence.
On the seventh day, march around Jericho seven times; on the seventh circuit, when the priests blew a long blast on the shofars, all the people shouted with a great shout.
Israel obeyed meticulously; on the seventh day at the great shout, the massive stone walls collapsed flat into the ground!
The army charged straight ahead, devoted the city to destruction as the firstfruits offering to God, and brought Rahab and her family out safely.
strengths: Instant, humble submission: dropped his sword and fell on his face the moment he recognized divine authority.
Absolute obedience to a militarily illogical battle plan, trusting God's supernatural power.
Faithfully honored his covenant oath to Rahab and her household.
failures: Scripture records no failure here; Jericho's fall stands as the supreme triumph of faith (Hebrews 11:30).

scripture.title: Circumcision at Gilgal, Passover, and the Commander of Yahweh's Army

verses.text: Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you.' Therefore the name of that place was called Gilgal, to this day.
The manna ceased on the next day, after they had eaten of the produce of the land. The children of Israel didn’t have manna any more; but they ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

When Joshua was by Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man stood in front of him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went to him, and said to him, 'Are you for us, or for our adversaries?'
He said, 'No; but I have come now as commander of Yahweh’s army.' Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and worshiped, and said to him, 'What does my lord say to his servant?'
The prince of Yahweh’s army said to Joshua, 'Take off your sandals from off your feet; for the place where you stand is holy.' Joshua did so.

scripture.title: The Seven-Day March, the Great Shout, the Wall Collapsing, and Rahab Rescued

verses.text: Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Behold, I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king, and the mighty men of valor.'
'All your men of war shall march around the city, going around the city once. You shall do this six days.'
'Seven priests shall bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark. On the seventh day, you shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.'

'It shall be that when they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; and the wall of the city will fall down flat, and the people shall go up every man straight before him.'
At the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, 'Shout, for Yahweh has given you the city!'

So the people shouted, and the priests blew the trumpets. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.
The young men the spies went in, and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that she had... and they set them outside of the camp of Israel.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Whose Side Is God On? The Sword of the Commander
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Joshua 5:13-14 records one of the most profound theological course-corrections in Scripture. General Joshua was walking near the massive, double-walled fortress of Jericho. He was studying the ramparts, planning siege strategies. Suddenly, a Man appeared standing in the path with a drawn sword in His hand! Joshua marched up like a courageous soldier and asked the natural human question: 'Are you for us, or for our adversaries?'

Listen to the shocking, one-word answer of the heavenly Warrior: **'NO!'** What a staggering answer! Joshua asked an either/or question: Are You on our side or their side? And the Commander answered: 'No!' That one word cuts through all our religious self-centeredness. We are constantly trying to enlist God into our causes, praying: 'Lord, bless my plans, endorse my political party, support my ambition, take my side!' And God looks down from heaven and says: 'No! I did not come to take sides; **I came to take over!**'

Notice who this Figure was: He was not a created angel, for when Joshua fell on his face and worshiped, the Figure received his worship! (When John tried to worship an angel in Revelation 19:10, the angel shouted: 'Don't do it! I am a fellow servant!'). Furthermore, this Commander commanded Joshua: 'Take off your sandals, for the place where you stand is holy ground'—the exact words Yahweh spoke from the burning bush! This was a Christophany: a pre-incarnate appearance of Jesus Christ as the supreme Commander of the armies of heaven.

And look at Joshua's response: he didn't argue. He dropped his sword, took off his sandals, fell face-first in the dust, and asked: 'What does my Lord say to His servant?' (v. 14). That is the posture of victory! When you surrender unconditionally to King Jesus, the battle is no longer yours; it is His. And when the battle belongs to God, even the impregnable walls of Jericho will collapse flat before Him.

lessons.lesson: Stop Asking God to Take Your Side; Surrender to His Leadership
lessons.detail: The Commander answered: 'No; but I have come as commander of Yahweh's army.' True discipleship is not getting God to bless our agendas, but laying down our swords and surrendering unconditionally to His lordship.
lessons.question: Are you trying to enlist God to bless your personal plans, or asking Him: 'What does my Lord say to His servant?'

lessons.lesson: God's Battle Strategies Defy Human Logic
lessons.detail: Marching silently around Jericho with the Ark and blowing rams' horns seemed foolish to military experts. God's spiritual weapons—prayer, praise, obedience, and truth—overcome fortified walls that human weapons cannot touch.
lessons.question: Are you fighting your spiritual battles with worldly weapons of anger and manipulation, or with prayer, worship, and obedience?

lessons.lesson: True Worship Precedes True Victory
lessons.detail: Before Jericho's walls fell, Joshua was on his face with sandals off on holy ground. The greatest preparation for any challenge is intimate, reverent worship at the feet of Jesus.
lessons.question: Do you spend as much time on your face in worship before God as you do worrying and strategizing about your obstacles?

lessons.lesson: Honor Every Promise with Impeccable Integrity
lessons.detail: Amidst the chaos of conquering a major city, Joshua ensured that Rahab and her entire household were brought out safely according to their oath. God's servants keep their promises with unwavering fidelity.
lessons.question: Are you known as a person of your word whose promises can be completely trusted even in chaotic circumstances?

quiz.question: What ceased the day after Israel celebrated Passover and ate the produce of Canaan in Joshua 5:12?
options: The pillar of cloud and fire
The sound of the silver trumpets
The flow of the Jordan River
quiz.explanation: Scripture explicitly states: 'The manna ceased on the next day, after they had eaten of the produce of the land.'

quiz.question: What did the Man with the drawn sword reply when Joshua asked 'Are you for us, or for our adversaries?' in Joshua 5:14?
options: 'I am an angel sent to help Joshua'
'No; but I have come now as commander of Yahweh’s army'
'I am a warrior of the wilderness'
quiz.explanation: He answered: 'No; but I have come now as commander of Yahweh’s army.'

quiz.question: What command did the Commander give Joshua in Joshua 5:15 that mirrored Moses at the burning bush?
options: 'Take off your sandals from off your feet; for the place where you stand is holy'
quiz.explanation: The prince of Yahweh's army said: 'Take off your sandals from off your feet; for the place where you stand is holy.' Joshua did so.

quiz.question: How many times did Israel march around Jericho on the seventh day before the walls fell in Joshua 6:4, 15?
quiz.explanation: On the seventh day, they marched around the city seven times.

quiz.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 11:30, the walls of Jericho fell down by faith, after they had been encircled for seven days.
quiz.explanation: True. Hebrews 11:30 explicitly declares: 'By faith, the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been encircled for seven days.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus Christ, You are the Supreme Commander of the armies of heaven! I take off the sandals of my self-will and fall on my face before Your holy presence. Forgive me for the foolish times I have treated You as an assistant to my plans, asking You to take my side rather than surrendering to Your sovereign command. I lay down my sword, my human strategies, and my anxious maneuvering at Your feet today. Speak, Lord, for Your servant listens! Give me the faith to march in obedience even when Your battle plans defy human logic. Bring down every fortified wall of fear, addiction, and impossibility in my life, not by human might, but by Your Holy Spirit. In Your victorious name, Amen.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Lord Jesus, Commander of heaven's army, I fall on my face before You; speak, for Your servant is listening.
closingPrayer.prompt: Drop to your knees in prayer, symbolically taking off your sandals, and say to Jesus: 'Lord, I surrender my agenda to You; what do You say to Your servant?'

75.season: The Hidden Sin in the Camp at Ai
75.theme: Secret sin in private brings public defeat and corporate devastation, while honest confession and radical removal of evil restores God's favor.

memoryVerse.text: Joshua said to Achan, 'My son, please give glory to Yahweh, the God of Israel, and make confession to him; and tell me now what you have done. Don’t hide it from me.'
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Hidden sin cannot stay buried; confessing our compromises gives glory to God by acknowledging His truth, while concealing sin leads to tragic ruin.

cramData.firstLetters: J s t A, 'M s, p g g t Y, t G o I, a m c t h; a t m n w y h d. D h i f m.'

profile.title: Achan: The Stolen Mantle and the Valley of Trouble
profile.who: Achan (son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah), who willfully violated God's explicit ban by stealing plunder from devoted Jericho—a beautiful Babylonian mantle, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold—bringing military defeat upon Israel at Ai and death upon his household.
profile.whenAndWhere: The camp of Gilgal, the battlefield of Ai, and the Valley of Achor, around 1406 BC.
profile.family: Achan, father Carmi, grandfather Zabdi, great-grandfather Zerah of the royal tribe of Judah; his sons, daughters, and livestock.
keyMoments: Before Jericho fell, Joshua strictly warned: 'Keep yourselves from the devoted thing, lest you make the camp of Israel accursed... all silver, gold, brass, and iron are holy to Yahweh; they shall go into the treasury.'
Achan saw among the ruins a luxurious woven Babylonian coat, 200 shekels of silver, and a 50-shekel bar of gold; he coveted them, took them, and buried them secretly inside his tent beneath the dirt.
Joshua sent three thousand soldiers to capture the small hilltop city of Ai; but the men of Ai routed Israel, chasing them from the gate and killing thirty-six men.
Israel's hearts melted like water; Joshua tore his clothes, fell face-down before the Ark until evening, and cried out in bewildered grief.

Yahweh spoke sharply: 'Get up! Why have you fallen on your face? Israel has sinned! They have even transgressed my covenant... they have stolen, and also lied, and put it among their own goods! Therefore the children of Israel can't stand before their enemies!'
God commanded a tribe-by-tribe, clan-by-clan, household-by-household investigation by lot in the morning.
The lot fell on the tribe of Judah, then the Zerahite clan, then Zabdi's household, and finally on Achan.
Joshua gently implored: 'My son, give glory to Yahweh, and make confession... tell me what you have done!'
Achan confessed: 'Truly I have sinned against Yahweh... When I saw... I coveted them, and took them; behold, they are hidden in the earth in the middle of my tent.'

Messengers ran to Achan's tent, dug up the stolen treasure, and poured it out before Yahweh; Israel took Achan, his family (accomplices in concealing the buried treasure), his oxen, and all his goods to the Valley of Achor ('Trouble') and stoned them with stones.
Repentant and cleansed, Israel advanced again against Ai with divine tactical ambush, burning the city and conquering the territory.
strengths: Honest final confession when confronted, acknowledging that he had sinned against Yahweh.
Demonstrated that God's justice is impartial, even toward the royal tribe of Judah.
failures: Blind, reckless greed: stole what was consecrated exclusively to God's treasury.
Lived with the buried lie for days while 36 innocent Hebrew soldiers died in battle.
Brought disgrace, military defeat, and destruction upon his entire family.

scripture.title: The Defeat at Ai, Joshua's Lament, Achan's Exposure and Judgment

verses.text: But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the devoted things; for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of the devoted things: and Yahweh’s anger burned against the children of Israel.
The men of Ai struck of them about thirty-six men... and the hearts of the people melted, and became like water.
Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Get up! Why have you fallen on your face?'

'Israel has sinned. Yes, they have even transgressed my covenant which I commanded them. Yes, they have even taken of the devoted things, and have also stolen, and also deceived, and they have even put it among their own stuff.'
Joshua said to Achan, 'My son, please give glory to Yahweh, the God of Israel, and make confession to him; and tell me now what you have done. Don’t hide it from me.'
Achan answered Joshua, and said, 'Truly I have sinned against Yahweh, the God of Israel, and this is what I have done:'

'When I saw among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them. Behold, they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it.'
Joshua said, 'Why have you troubled us? Yahweh will trouble you today.' All Israel stoned him with stones; and they burned them with fire, and stoned them with stones.
They raised over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. Yahweh turned from the fierceness of his anger. Therefore the name of that place was called 'The valley of Achor' to this day.

scripture.title: Ai Conquered by Ambush and the Altar of Blessings at Mount Ebal

verses.text: Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Don’t be afraid, neither be dismayed. Take all the people of war with you, and arise, go up to Ai. Behold, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, with his people, his city, and his land.'
Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai; for I will give it into your hand.' Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
The ambush arose quickly out of their place, and they ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand, and entered into the city, and took it. They hurried and set the city on fire.
Then Joshua built an altar to Yahweh, the God of Israel, in Mount Ebal,
Afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: The Dirt Floor of the Tent: The Lie That Sin Can Be Private
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Joshua 7 delivers one of the most sobering moral warnings in the entire Old Testament. Fresh off the miraculous, wall-flattening victory at Jericho, Israel marched up to the modest, small hilltop city of Ai. The spies said: 'Don’t weary all the people; send only two or three thousand men, for the people of Ai are few!' (v. 3). But instead of an easy victory, Israel was routed in humiliated panic, and thirty-six soldiers were killed. Joshua fell on his face in bewildered grief, crying: 'Lord, what will become of Your great Name?'

Listen to God's abrupt, thunderous reply: 'Get up! Why have you fallen on your face? Israel has sinned!... There is an accursed thing in your midst!' (vv. 10-13). Notice the principle: **You cannot pray away what you need to repent of!** Joshua was praying, weeping, and fasting, but God said: 'Stop praying and start purifying! As long as there is secret, harbored sin in the camp, My presence cannot fight for you.'

Look at Achan's confession in verse 21. Trace the deadly anatomy of temptation that has snared human souls from Eve in Eden to David in Jerusalem: **'I saw... I coveted... I took... and they are hidden!'** Notice that progression: first the gaze of the eye, then the spark of desire in the heart, then the physical theft with the hand, and finally the desperate cover-up under the dirt floor of the tent! Achan thought: 'Nobody saw me. It's just a coat and some gold buried in the dirt under my sleeping mat. Who does it hurt?'

It cost the lives of thirty-six Hebrew soldiers! It broke the heart of Joshua! It shattered his own family! **There is no such thing as private sin.** Secret compromise in your life leaks out into your family, your church, and your relationships. Yet notice God's redemptive promise in Hosea 2:15: 'I will give her the Valley of Achor [Trouble] for a door of hope!' When you dig up the secret sin, confess it honestly, and bring it into the light of the cross, the valley of your greatest trouble becomes a door of glorious hope and victory.

lessons.lesson: There Is No Such Thing as 'Victimless' or 'Private' Sin
lessons.detail: Achan's hidden theft brought defeat upon the entire army and cost 36 soldiers their lives. Secret compromise in our private lives always poisons our spiritual influence and damages the people we love.
lessons.question: Is there a hidden compromise or habit in your life that you have falsely rationalized as 'not hurting anyone else'?

lessons.lesson: Prayer Cannot Substitute for Necessary Repentance
lessons.detail: God told Joshua to get up off his face because prayer cannot fix a problem that requires confession and moral purification. When God convicts you of sin, stop endlessly talking about it—confess it and remove it.
lessons.question: Are you praying for God's blessings and breakthrough while refusing to deal with a specific area of disobedience?

lessons.lesson: Guard Your Heart at the Point of 'Seeing' and 'Coveting'
lessons.detail: Achan's fall followed the pattern: I saw, I coveted, I took, I hid. Cut off temptation at the first step; take captive what your eyes look upon before desire conceives into sinful action.
lessons.question: What visual media, websites, or material desires do you need to guard your eyes against today to prevent covetousness?

lessons.lesson: God Turns the Valley of Achor into a Door of Hope
lessons.detail: Achor means 'Trouble.' When we stop concealing our failures and bring them honestly to Christ, God transforms our darkest valleys of failure into doors of fresh hope and restoration.
lessons.question: Have you brought your hidden failures into the light of Christ's forgiveness, allowing Him to turn your trouble into hope?

quiz.question: What specific items did Achan steal and hide in his tent from devoted Jericho in Joshua 7:21?
options: A royal chariot and bronze armor
A beautiful Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels of silver, and a fifty-shekel wedge of gold
Two barrels of Canaanite wine and fine flour
quiz.explanation: Achan confessed: 'When I saw among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them.'

quiz.question: How many Israelite soldiers were killed during the first battle of Ai in Joshua 7:5?
quiz.explanation: Scripture explicitly states: 'The men of Ai struck of them about thirty-six men...'

quiz.question: What did God tell Joshua when Joshua fell on his face weeping before the Ark in Joshua 7:10?
options: 'Get up! Why have you fallen on your face? Israel has sinned!'
quiz.explanation: Yahweh said to Joshua: 'Get up! Why have you fallen on your face? Israel has sinned...'

quiz.question: What does the name of the valley where Achan was judged, 'Achor,' mean in Hebrew?
quiz.explanation: Joshua asked 'Why have you troubled us?' and the valley was named Achor, meaning 'Trouble'.

quiz.question: True or False: In Hosea 2:15, the prophet promises that God will transform the Valley of Achor (Trouble) into a door of hope.
quiz.explanation: True. Hosea 2:15 declares: 'I will give her... the valley of Achor for a door of hope.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of holiness, from whom no secret is hidden and before whose eyes all things are naked and bare! Search my heart today, O God, and know my thoughts; try me, and know my anxious ways, and see if there be any wicked way in me. Forgive me for the foolish delusion that sin can ever be private or buried under the dirt floor of my life. Cleanse me from hidden covetousness, secret compromise, and double-minded deceit. I bring every hidden failure into the healing light of the cross of Jesus Christ. Thank You that You do not leave me in condemnation, but turn my Valley of Achor into a door of living hope and victory. Give me clean hands, a pure heart, and undivided integrity before You. In Jesus' holy name, Amen.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Lord, I give glory to You and make honest confession; search my tent and cleanse my heart from all hidden compromise.
closingPrayer.prompt: Ask the Holy Spirit to reveal if there is anything buried in the 'tent' of your private life that needs to be brought into the light of God's forgiveness.

76.season: Failing to Ask Counsel of the Lord
76.theme: Relying on human sensory logic rather than seeking God's counsel leads into deceptive traps, yet God honors covenant integrity even when made under deceit.

memoryVerse.text: The men sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Our greatest spiritual blunders often occur not when facing obvious roaring lions, but when subtle deceptions appeal to our eyes and we fail to seek God's counsel in prayer.

cramData.firstLetters: T m s t p, a d a c f Y m.

profile.title: The Gibeonites: The Moldy Bread and the Deceptive Treaty
profile.who: The Hivite citizens of Gibeon, a major royal city near Jerusalem, who realized they could not defeat Israel militarily, executing an elaborate disguise of worn sandals and dry, moldy bread to trick Joshua into a binding non-aggression covenant.
profile.whenAndWhere: Gilgal and the hill country of Gibeon (Benjamin), around 1406 BC.
profile.family: The four Hivite cities: Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.
keyMoments: After the destruction of Jericho and Ai, the kings of Canaan banded together for war; but the leaders of Gibeon acted with shrewd cunning.
Loaded their donkeys with worn sacks, cracked and mended wineskins, patched sandals, old clothes, and dry, moldy bread.
Arrived at Joshua's camp at Gilgal claiming to be ambassadors from a distant, faraway country outside Canaan who had heard of the fame of Yahweh.
Joshua and the princes questioned them, touched their dry crumbly bread, inspected their cracked wineskins, and evaluated their story using human logic alone.
Scripture inserts the devastating verdict: 'The men sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth.'
Joshua made peace with them and the princes swore a covenant of mutual defense, ratified before Yahweh.
Three days later, the truth emerged: the Gibeonites were close neighbors living only a one-day march away in the heart of Canaan!
The congregation grumbled against the leaders, but Joshua and the princes held firm: 'We have sworn to them by Yahweh... we may not touch them lest wrath be on us!'
Joshua honored the treaty, but assigned the Gibeonites to perpetual service as woodcutters and water-carriers for the congregation and for the altar of Yahweh.
When five Amorite kings attacked Gibeon for making peace with Israel, Joshua marched all night to defend his new treaty partners, honoring his sworn word.
strengths: The Gibeonites possessed healthy fear and reverence for the God of Israel, choosing servitude over idolatrous annihilation.
Joshua and the princes demonstrated absolute covenant integrity by refusing to break their sworn oath even after discovering the fraud.
failures: Joshua and the leaders relied on sensory evidence (sight, touch, taste) and failed to consult Yahweh through the Urim and Thummim before signing the treaty.

scripture.title: The Gibeonite Deception, Moldy Bread, and the Binding Treaty

verses.text: But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,
they also resorted to a ruse, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks on their donkeys, and old, torn-up, and bound-up wineskins,
and old and patched sandals on their feet, and wore old garments on them. All the bread of their food supply was dry and moldy.

'Our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spoke to us, saying, "Take provisions in your hand for the journey, and go to meet them, and tell them, 'We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.'"'
The men sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth.
Joshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them, to let them live. The princes of the congregation swore to them.
At the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were their neighbors, and that they lived among them.
But all the princes said to all the congregation, 'We have sworn to them by Yahweh, the God of Israel: now therefore we may not touch them.'
That day Joshua made them wood cutters and water drawers for the congregation, and for Yahweh’s altar, to this day, in the place which he should choose.

scripture.title: Five Amorite Kings Attack Gibeon and Joshua Defends His Treaty Partners

verses.text: Now when Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai... and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and were among them,
they were very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
Therefore the five kings of the Amorites... gathered themselves together, and went up, they and all their armies, and encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it.
The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua to the camp at Gilgal, saying, 'Don’t abandon your servants! Come up to us quickly, and save us, and help us;'
So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he, and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.
Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Don’t fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands. Not a man of them will stand before you.'

whatGodIsSaying.headline: The Moldy Bread Test: When Common Sense Bypasses Prayer
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Joshua 9 exposes one of the most subtle traps in the spiritual life. Notice how the enemy came against Israel: In chapter 6 at Jericho, the enemy was a towering wall. In chapter 7 at Ai, the enemy was a fierce counter-attack. But in chapter 9, the enemy did not come with chariots, swords, or threatening shouts. The enemy arrived as humble, weary travelers wearing dusty rags, limping in patched sandals, offering dry, moldy bread, and speaking pious words about the glory of Yahweh!

Look at verse 14—one of the most searching sentences in the Old Testament: 'The men sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth.' Joshua and the leaders used their eyes: the bread looked moldy. They used their hands: the wineskins felt cracked. They used their tongues: the crumbs tasted dry. They used their human logic: everything seemed to match the travelers' story. But they made one catastrophic omission: **they didn't pray!** They relied on their own sensory common sense instead of seeking God's counsel. When an opportunity looks obvious and sensible, that is precisely when we must hit our knees and inquire of the Lord.

Yet notice the inspiring sequel in verses 19-20. When the deception was discovered three days later, the leaders did not tear up the contract or slaughter the Gibeonites. They said: 'We have sworn to them by Yahweh, and we will not touch them!' God honors a person who 'swears to his own hurt and does not change' (Psalm 15:4). When you give your word in the Name of God, keep it even when it costs you. And look at what Joshua did with Gibeon: he made them woodcutters and water-carriers for the altar of Yahweh. Centered near God's presence, the Gibeonites were integrated into worship, and centuries later during the rebuild of Jerusalem, Gibeonites faithfully helped Nehemiah repair the walls (Nehemiah 3:7)! God redeems even our blunders when we walk in covenant integrity.

lessons.lesson: Never Rely on Human Senses over Seeking God's Counsel
lessons.detail: Israel evaluated the Gibeonites by sight, taste, and touch, but neglected to ask God. Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding; in all your ways acknowledge Him.
lessons.question: Are you currently making a major decision based merely on common sense without stopping to seek God's counsel in prayer?

lessons.lesson: Covenant Integrity Demands Keeping Your Word Even When Costly
lessons.detail: Even though tricked, Israel refused to break their sworn oath. A godly person keeps their word and fulfills their commitments even when it turns out to be disadvantageous or inconvenient.
lessons.question: Have you made a promise or commitment that has become difficult or costly, and will you honor your word with godly integrity?

lessons.lesson: The Enemy Often Attacks Through Subtle Deception Rather than Open War
lessons.detail: Satan does not always attack like a roaring lion; he frequently disguises himself as an angel of light. Be spiritually vigilant when flatterers arrive speaking pious religious phrases.
lessons.question: Are you testing the spiritual spirits and advice around you against the plumb line of God's Word and prayer?

lessons.lesson: God Honors Faithfulness to Defend Those We Have Pledged to Help
lessons.detail: When Gibeon was attacked, Joshua marched all night to defend them. God blessed Joshua's loyalty, telling him: 'Don't fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands.' Honor your obligations with swift, faithful loyalty.
lessons.question: Whom have you pledged to support or protect, and how can you stand faithfully by their side in their time of trouble?

quiz.question: What ruse did the Gibeonites use to deceive Joshua in Joshua 9:4-5?
options: They sent gold from Egypt and pretended to be royal princes
They took old sacks, torn wineskins, patched sandals, old clothes, and dry, moldy bread
They wore disguise masks of sheepskin
They claimed to be descendants of Joseph
quiz.explanation: They used old sacks, torn and mended wineskins, patched sandals, worn garments, and dry, moldy bread.

quiz.question: What fatal mistake did the leaders of Israel make in Joshua 9:14?
options: They refused to take any provisions
They sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth
They lost the Ark of the Covenant
They fell asleep on guard duty
quiz.explanation: Scripture explicitly records: 'The men sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth.'

quiz.question: How long after making the treaty did Israel discover the Gibeonites were actually close neighbors in Joshua 9:16?
quiz.explanation: At the end of three days after making the covenant, they heard that they were close neighbors.

quiz.question: What perpetual role did Joshua assign to the Gibeonites in Joshua 9:27?
options: Wood cutters and water drawers for the congregation and for Yahweh’s altar
Keepers of the sheep of Judah
quiz.explanation: Joshua made them wood cutters and water drawers for the congregation and for Yahweh's altar.

quiz.question: True or False: In Joshua 10:6-8, when five Amorite kings attacked Gibeon, Joshua refused to help them because Gibeon had lied about the moldy bread.
quiz.explanation: False. Joshua honored his treaty, marched all night with his army, and God gave them a massive victory.

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of all wisdom, You search every motive and see through every disguise. Forgive me for the foolish times I have sampled the provisions of this world, relying on my own eyes, taste, and logic while failing to ask counsel from Your mouth in prayer. Deliver me from the arrogance of common sense that bypasses intimacy with You. Teach me to pause before every decision, contract, partnership, and relationship, inquiring of Your Spirit. Give me the unyielding integrity of Joshua to keep my word and honor my commitments even when it proves inconvenient or costly. Redeem my past blunders, and weave my life into the service of Your altar. In Jesus' name, Amen.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Lord, teach me to seek counsel from Your mouth before every decision, walking in prayer and covenant integrity.
closingPrayer.prompt: Pause and present any decision, contract, or relationship before God right now, asking for His counsel from His mouth.

77.season: The Day the Sun Stood Still at Gibeon
77.theme: God fights supernaturally for His people, answering the audacious prayers of faith that dare to ask for the impossible.

memoryVerse.text: There was no day like that before it or after it, that Yahweh listened to the voice of a man; for Yahweh fought for Israel.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Joshua's prayer for the sun to stand still reveals that when we are in alignment with God's redemptive mission, God commands the very cosmos to fight on our behalf.

cramData.firstLetters: T w n d l t b i o a i, t Y l t t v o a m; f Y f f I.

profile.title: Joshua: The General Who Commanded the Sun to Stand Still
profile.who: Joshua, marching all night from Gilgal to rescue besieged Gibeon from an alliance of five Amorite kings, unleashing torrential hailstones and praying the most audacious astronomical prayer in world history.
profile.whenAndWhere: The ascent of Beth Horon and the Valley of Aijalon in central Canaan, around 1406 BC.
profile.family: Joshua, the warrior army of Israel, fighting on behalf of Gibeon.
keyMoments: Five Amorite kings (Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, Eglon) formed a coalition and besieged Gibeon; Gibeon sent a desperate plea to Joshua at Gilgal.
Joshua marched his entire army all night uphill from Gilgal, launching a surprise attack at dawn.
Yahweh threw the Amorite armies into total confusion before Israel, cutting them down with great slaughter.
As the Amorites fled down the descent of Beth Horon, Yahweh cast down colossal hailstones from heaven upon them; more died from the hailstones than by the swords of Israel.
Daylight was running out, and the broken enemy forces would escape in the darkness of the mountain ravines.
Filled with the Holy Spirit and audacious faith, Joshua spoke to Yahweh in the sight of all Israel: 'Sun, stand still on Gibeon; and you, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon!'
The sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and didn't hurry to set for about a whole day, until the nation avenged themselves on their enemies.
Recorded in the Book of Jashar: 'There was no day like that before it or after it, that Yahweh listened to the voice of a man; for Yahweh fought for Israel.'
The five kings hid in a cave at Makkedah; Joshua rolled stones over the mouth until the battle finished, then executed them and hung their bodies on trees until sunset.
Conquered the entire southern hill country, from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, because 'Yahweh, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.'
strengths: Relentless physical and spiritual endurance: marched all night up steep mountain terrain to honor a treaty.
Audacious, mountain-moving prayer: dared to ask God for unprecedented cosmic intervention.
Gave 100% of the glory to God, recognizing that 'Yahweh fought for Israel.'
failures: Scripture records no failure in this campaign; it stands as one of the greatest military chapters in biblical history.

scripture.title: The All-Night March, Heavenly Hailstones, and the Sun Standing Still

verses.text: Joshua therefore came on them suddenly. He marched from Gilgal all night.
Yahweh confused them before Israel, and he killed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth Horon, and struck them to Azekah, and to Makkedah.

As they fled from before Israel, while they were at the descent of Beth Horon, Yahweh cast down great stones from the sky on them to Azekah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than who the children of Israel killed with the sword.

Then Joshua spoke to Yahweh in the day when Yahweh delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel; and he said in the sight of Israel, 'Sun, stand still on Gibeon; and you, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon!'

The sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies. Isn’t this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and didn’t hurry to go down about a whole day.
There was no day like that before it or after it, that Yahweh listened to the voice of a man; for Yahweh fought for Israel.
Joshua took all these kings and their land at one time, because Yahweh, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.

scripture.title: Northern Kings Defeated at the Waters of Merom and the Land Rested

verses.text: They went out, they and all their armies with them, many people, even as the sand that is on the seashore in multitude, with very many horses and chariots.

Yahweh said to Joshua, 'Don’t be afraid because of them; for tomorrow at this time, I will deliver them up all slain before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses, and burn their chariots with fire.'
So Joshua came, and all the people of war with him, against them by the waters of Merom suddenly, and fell on them.
Yahweh delivered them into the hand of Israel... and they struck them, until they left them no one remaining.

So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that Yahweh spoke to Moses; and Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. Then the land had rest from war.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: The Audacity of Sun-Stopping Prayer: When Heaven Listens to a Man
whatGodIsSaying.reflection:
Look at the extraordinary scene in Joshua 10:12-14. Joshua had marched his men uphill all night from Gilgal. They engaged five combined armies, pursued them down the rocky passes of Beth Horon, and watched God hurl massive, targeted hailstones from heaven. But the sun was sinking rapidly behind the hills of Aijalon, and shadows were lengthening over the valleys. If night fell, the enemy would slip away into the caves and mountain clefts, regroup, and drag out a war that could last for years.

Joshua did something that had never been done in human history: in the sight of all Israel, he looked up into the sky and commanded the celestial bodies: 'Sun, stand still on Gibeon! And you, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon!' (v. 12). Think of the sheer, breathtaking audacity of that prayer! Joshua did not ask for a minor blessing or comfortable provision; he asked the Creator of the universe to suspend the rotation of the earth!

And look at verse 14: 'There was no day like that before it or after it, that Yahweh listened to the voice of a man; for Yahweh fought for Israel!' The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed its setting for about a full day! Why did God honor such a wild, impossible prayer? Because Joshua was not praying for selfish vanity, personal fame, or parlor tricks; Joshua was in absolute alignment with the redemptive mission of God! When you are fighting God's battles, doing God's work, and standing for God's covenant, heaven backs your prayers with limitless cosmic authority. Jesus told us in Mark 11:23: 'Whoever says to this mountain, "Be taken up and cast into the sea," and doesn’t doubt in his heart... he will have whatever he says!' Stop praying small, safe, predictable prayers; dare to pray sun-stopping prayers for the advance of God's kingdom!

lessons.lesson: Dare to Pray Audacious, Kingdom-Aligning Prayers
lessons.detail: Joshua asked God to stop the sun and moon, and God answered. When our prayers align with God's mission, we can ask for supernatural intervention that defies human impossibility.
lessons.question: What is the biggest, boldest prayer you are currently bringing before God, and does it align with His kingdom glory?

lessons.lesson: God Fights for Those Who Keep Covenant and Walk in Faith
lessons.detail: More enemies died from divine hailstones than by the sword. God fought for Israel because they were walking in obedience. When you walk in covenant faithfulness, God takes responsibility for fighting your battles.
lessons.question: Are you striving in your own human strength, or resting in the truth that the Lord of hosts is fighting for you?

lessons.lesson: Combine Diligent Human Effort with Complete Divine Reliance
lessons.detail: Joshua did not sit passively waiting for a miracle; he marched his men all night in an exhausting uphill trek, and *then* prayed for the sun to stand still. Faith works hard while trusting God completely for the supernatural outcome.
lessons.question: Are you balancing diligent preparation and hard work with dependent prayer for God's supernatural power?

lessons.lesson: Do Not Fear Multitudes of Chariots and Worldly Armies
lessons.detail: When northern kings assembled armies 'as the sand on the seashore' with countless chariots, God told Joshua: 'Don't be afraid.' Numbers and worldly resources mean nothing to the God who commands the universe.
lessons.question: How does the victory at the Waters of Merom give you peace when you feel outnumbered or outmatched by worldly forces?

quiz.question: What did Yahweh cast down from the sky upon the fleeing Amorite army at Beth Horon in Joshua 10:11?
options: Great stones (hailstones) from the sky, killing more than died by the sword
quiz.explanation: Yahweh cast down great stones (hailstones) from heaven, and more died from the hailstones than by the sword.

quiz.question: What audacious command did Joshua speak in the sight of all Israel in Joshua 10:12?
options: 'Mountains of Canaan, fall into the sea!'
'Sun, stand still on Gibeon; and you, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon!'
quiz.explanation: Joshua cried: 'Sun, stand still on Gibeon; and you, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon!'

quiz.question: How long did the sun delay its setting according to Joshua 10:13?
quiz.explanation: Scripture states: 'The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and didn’t hurry to go down about a whole day.'

quiz.question: True or False: According to Joshua 10:14, there was no day like that before it or after it, that Yahweh listened to the voice of a man, for Yahweh fought for Israel.
quiz.explanation: True. Joshua 10:14 explicitly declares this unique divine intervention.

quiz.question: Where did the five Amorite kings hide before being discovered in Joshua 10:16-17?
quiz.explanation: The five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of angel armies, Creator of the sun, the moon, and the stellar heavens! You are the God who listens to the prayers of Your servants and fights for Your people. Forgive me for the smallness of my prayers and the timidity of my faith. Enlarge my vision today! Deliver me from praying only safe, predictable prayers that require no supernatural intervention. Give me the holy boldness of Joshua to march through the night in faithful obedience, and to pray sun-stopping, mountain-moving prayers for the glory of Your Name and the advance of Your kingdom. Remind my soul that no coalition of darkness, no obstacle, and no army can stand before You, for Yahweh, the God of Israel, fights for His people. In Jesus' mighty name, Amen.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Lord, You fight for Your people; hear the audacious prayers of my heart today and reveal Your mighty power.
closingPrayer.prompt: Bring your most impossible, mountain-sized need before God in prayer right now, daring to ask Him for a 'sun-stopping' breakthrough.

78.season: 'Give Me This Mountain': Lionhearted at Eighty-Five
78.theme: Wholehearted faith in God's promises defies age, fatigue, and giant obstacles to conquer territory for God's glory.

memoryVerse.text: Now therefore give me this hill country, of which Yahweh spoke in that day... It may be that Yahweh will be with me, and I shall drive them out, as Yahweh said.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: At age eighty-five, Caleb did not ask for a comfortable retirement or an easy valley; he asked for the mountain infested with giants, proving that wholehearted faith never retires.

cramData.firstLetters: N t g m t h c, o w Y s i t d... I m b t Y w b w m, a I s d t o, a Y s.

profile.title: Caleb: The Eighty-Five-Year-Old Giant Slayer of Hebron
profile.who: Caleb (son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, of the tribe of Judah), who forty-five years after bringing the good report from Kadesh-barnea, stood before Joshua at age eighty-five with undiminished physical vigor and spiritual zeal, asking for the toughest mountain in Canaan—Hebron, home of the terrifying Anakim giants.
profile.whenAndWhere: Gilgal and the rugged hill country of Hebron (Kiriath Arba), around 1400 BC.
profile.family: Caleb; daughter Achsah; nephew and future first judge of Israel, Othniel; tribe of Judah.
keyMoments: Forty-five years after the spy mission at Kadesh-barnea, land division commenced; Caleb stepped forward before Joshua at Gilgal.
Recounted Moses' oath: 'Because you have followed Yahweh my God fully, the land on which your foot has trodden will be an inheritance to you and to your children forever.'
Declared with blazing spiritual vigor: 'Behold, Yahweh has kept me alive, as he said, these forty-five years... and now, behold, I am eighty-five years old today!'
Testified of God's sustaining grace: 'I am as strong today as I was on the day that Moses sent me! As my strength was then, even so is my strength now for war, both to go out and to come in.'

Made his legendary request: 'Now therefore give me this hill country [mountain]... for you heard in that day how the Anakim were there, and great and fortified cities. It may be that Yahweh will be with me, and I shall drive them out, as Yahweh said!'
Joshua blessed Caleb and gave him Hebron for an inheritance, because he wholly followed Yahweh, the God of Israel.
Caleb marched up the mountain, drove out the three terrifying giant sons of Anak (Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai), and conquered the fortified city.
Offered his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever captured Kiriath Sepher (Debir); his nephew Othniel captured it.
Achsah boldly asked Caleb for a blessing: 'You have set me in the land of the South; give me also springs of water.' Caleb generously gave her both the upper springs and the lower springs.
strengths: Unwavering, wholehearted devotion maintained across forty-five years of desert waiting.
Refused the entitlement of an easy retirement; chose the hardest battleground to magnify God's power.
