quiz.explanation: David sings: 'I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus Christ, You are my Good Shepherd, and in You I lack nothing. Thank You for laying down Your holy life on the cross to rescue me from the jaws of the enemy. Thank You that You know my name, call me into Your fold, and lead me beside the quiet waters of Your peace. Forgive me for listening to the tempting voices of strangers or wandering away in anxiety. Today I rest secure in Your pierced hands, knowing that Your Father and You hold me with an unbreakable grip that no power in hell can sever. Guide my steps in paths of righteousness for Your name's sake.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Rest your heart in the double grip of the Father and the Son: surrender your biggest fear into the Shepherd's hands.

263.season: The One Thing Needed: Sitting at the Master's Feet
263.theme: Intimate communion with Christ at His feet is the one essential foundation for all fruitful service.

memoryVerse.text: “but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Activity for Jesus can easily degenerate into anxious resentment if we neglect the primary priority of sitting quietly at His feet to hear His word.

cramData.firstLetters: “b o t i n. M h c t g p, w w n b t a f h.”

profile.title: Martha and Mary of Bethany: The Distracted Hostess and the Contemplative Disciple
profile.who: Two sisters living in Bethany, two miles east of Jerusalem, who welcomed Jesus into their home; while Martha was overwhelmed with frantic culinary preparations and complained of Mary's lack of help, Mary sat peacefully at Jesus' feet drinking in His teaching, prompting Christ's immortal diagnosis of the 'one thing needed.'
profile.whenAndWhere: Bethany (near Jerusalem), Judea, circa AD 29.
profile.family: Sisters of Lazarus of Bethany; close personal friends of Jesus.
keyMoments: Martha welcomed Jesus into her home with genuine, hospitable love.
Her sister Mary sat at Jesus' feet (the traditional posture of a rabbinic student/disciple) and listened to His word.
Martha was distracted (periespato—dragged in circles) about much serving, becoming internally frazzled, anxious, and resentful.
Approached Jesus and interrupted with frustration: 'Lord, don't you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Tell her therefore to help me!'
Notice the subtle shift: Martha's service for Jesus had turned into complaining against Jesus and judging her sister.

Jesus answered her with profound tenderness and double repetition: 'Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things. But one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.'
Jesus did not condemn hospitality or meal preparation, but rebuked the anxious distraction that crowded out intimate communion with Him.
Affirmed Mary's radical counter-cultural choice: in first-century culture, women were excluded from formal rabbinic study, but Jesus defended her right to sit as a disciple at His feet.
Fulfilled Psalm 27:4: 'One thing I have asked of Yahweh, that I will seek after: that I may dwell in Yahweh's house all the days of my life, to see Yahweh's beauty, and to inquire in his temple.'
strengths: Martha's generous hospitality, leadership in the home, and deep affection for Jesus.
Mary's spiritual discernment: prioritizing eternal words over temporary chores.
Both grew in deep faith and love for Christ.
failures: Martha allowed busy ministry to breed anxious bitterness and critical judgment of others.

scripture.title: Mary at the Feet of Jesus and Martha's Distraction

verses.text: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word.
But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don't you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”
Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things.”
“But one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

scripture.title: One Thing Desired: To Behold the Beauty of Yahweh

verses.text: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
One thing I have asked of Yahweh, that I will seek after: that I may dwell in Yahweh's house all the days of my life, to see Yahweh's beauty, and to inquire in his temple.
When you said, “Seek my face,” my heart said to you, “I will seek your face, Yahweh.”

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Service for Christ Must Never Crowd Out Communion with Christ
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: The tragedy of Martha was not that she was doing something evil. Preparing a meal for Jesus and His disciples was a beautiful, loving act! Her danger was subtle: she was 'distracted with much serving.' The Greek word means being dragged in all directions at once. When our to-do list becomes our master, service for Jesus turns into anxiety, exhaustion, and resentment toward others: 'Lord, don't You care that my sister left me to serve alone?' The moment our serving makes us bitter, critical, or anxious, we have lost the heart of discipleship! Jesus looked at her with tears of affection: 'Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things. But ONE THING is needed.' What is that one thing? Sitting at the feet of Jesus, drinking in His word, and beholding His beauty. Before you can serve effectively with Martha's hands, you must first sit with Mary's heart.

lessons.lesson: Beware of Ministry Without Devotion
lessons.detail: When serving Jesus replaces spending time with Jesus, work for God quickly degenerates into resentment toward others.
lessons.question: Is your service in church or family producing joy, or are you becoming exhausted, bitter, and resentful?

lessons.lesson: Only 'One Thing' Is Truly Essential
lessons.detail: While life presents a thousand pressing demands, Jesus declares that intimate communion at His feet is the sole indispensable priority.
lessons.question: Does your daily schedule reflect that sitting at Jesus' feet is your primary, non-negotiable priority?

lessons.lesson: The Good Part Cannot Be Taken Away
lessons.detail: Cooked meals are eaten and dishes get dirty again, but the spiritual words absorbed at Jesus' feet are an eternal treasure that lasts forever.
lessons.question: Are you investing the best hours of your day into eternal spiritual nourishment or temporary chores?

lessons.lesson: Seek His Face Above All Else
lessons.detail: Like David in Psalm 27, make your life's singular pursuit beholding the beauty of the Lord and inquiring in His presence.
lessons.question: How can you simplify your life and quiet your mind so that you can genuinely 'seek His face' today?

263.notesPrompt: Examine your current lifestyle. Are you living more like 'distracted Martha' or 'listening Mary'? What practical adjustments can you make to protect unhurried time at the feet of Jesus?

quiz.question: What was Mary doing while Martha was preparing the meal in Luke 10:39?
options: Sitting at Jesus' feet and hearing His word
quiz.explanation: Luke 10:39 states that Mary 'sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word.'

quiz.question: What complaint did Martha bring to Jesus in Luke 10:40?
options: The disciples had tracked mud into the house
Lord, don't you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me
There was no wine left for dinner
quiz.explanation: Martha said: 'Lord, don't you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.'

quiz.question: How did Jesus gently diagnose Martha's internal condition in Luke 10:41?
options: Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things
You need to move to Jerusalem
quiz.explanation: Jesus answered: 'Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things.'

quiz.question: What did Jesus say about Mary's choice in Luke 10:42?
options: She is lazy and needs to help in the kitchen
One thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her
quiz.explanation: Jesus said: 'One thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.'

quiz.question: True or False: According to Psalm 27:4, David asked for ten thousand talents of gold above all other things.
quiz.explanation: False. David asked for one thing: to dwell in the house of Yahweh all the days of his life to behold His beauty and inquire in His temple.

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Gentle Master and Guest of my heart, forgive me for the frantic distraction that so easily fills my days. How often I become like Martha: anxious, troubled about many things, and resentful toward others, while neglecting the one thing that truly matters. Teach me to sit quietly at Your feet like Mary. Let me drink in Your life-giving words. Reorder my daily priorities so that my service springs from intimate communion, and my soul finds its rest in beholding Your beauty.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: One thing is needed: to sit at Your feet and hear Your word; help me choose the good part that will never be taken away.
closingPrayer.prompt: Pause all activity for ten minutes today, sit quietly with an open Bible at the feet of Jesus, and let Him speak to your heart.

264.season: Go and Do Likewise: Mercy on the Jericho Road
264.theme: Mercy crosses religious and racial barriers to bandage the bleeding neighbor left by the roadside.

memoryVerse.text: He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: True love for God is proved not by theoretical theological debates, but by active, costly mercy that crosses boundaries to bandage the wounded.

cramData.firstLetters: H s, “H w s m o h.” T J s t h, “G a d l.”

profile.title: The Good Samaritan: The Hero of the Jericho Road and Mirror of Christ
profile.who: In response to an expert in the Mosaic Law who sought to justify himself by asking 'And who is my neighbor?', Jesus told the immortal parable of a traveler stripped, beaten, and left half-dead on the dangerous seventeen-mile road from Jerusalem to Jericho; while a priest and a Levite crossed to the other side, a despised Samaritan stopped, showed compassion, bandaged his wounds with oil and wine, and paid for his full recovery.
profile.whenAndWhere: The road descending from Jerusalem to Jericho (the 'Adummim' or Ascent of Blood), circa AD 29.
profile.family: A despised Samaritan traveler; contrasting with the holy Jewish religious establishment.
keyMoments: A lawyer stood up and tested Jesus: 'Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?' Jesus pointed to the Law: love God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind, and love your neighbor as yourself.
Seeking to limit his moral responsibility, the lawyer asked: 'And who is my neighbor?'
Jesus answered with the Parable of the Good Samaritan: a man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who stripped him, beat him, and departed, leaving him half-dead.
By chance a certain priest came down that road; seeing the dying man, he passed by on the other side (perhaps fearing ritual defilement from a corpse under Numbers 19:11).
Likewise a Levite came to the place, looked at him, and passed by on the other side.
A certain Samaritan—a member of a despised, half-breed race hated by Jews—journeyed, came where he was, and saw him, and was moved with deep compassion.
Went to him, poured in oil (soothing) and wine (disinfecting), bandaged his wounds, set him on his own beast, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The next morning, took out two denarii (two days' wages), gave them to the innkeeper: 'Take care of him. Whatever more you spend, when I come back, I will repay you.'
Jesus asked the lawyer: 'Which of these three, do you think, seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?'
The lawyer couldn't even bring his lips to utter the word 'Samaritan', answering: 'He who showed mercy on him.' Jesus said: 'Go and do likewise.'
strengths: Unrestricted compassion that saw a human being in agony rather than an ethnic enemy.
Costly, practical generosity: poured out expensive oil, wine, time, his own donkey, and personal funds.
Open-ended commitment to the victim's complete rehabilitation.
failures: None in the parable; a radiant reflection of the heart of Jesus Christ Himself.

scripture.title: The Parable of the Good Samaritan

verses.text: Jesus answered, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.”
“By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.”
“In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place, and saw him, passed by on the other side.”
“But a certain Samaritan, as he travelled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,”
“came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.”
“On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, and gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I return.’”
“Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”

scripture.title: Do Not Withhold Good from the Needy

verses.text: Don't withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.
Don't say to your neighbor, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it,” when you have it by you.
Don't let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Christ Is the True Good Samaritan Who Bound Up Our Wounds and Paid Our Full Ransom
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: The lawyer wanted to debate definitions: 'Who is my neighbor?' He wanted a loophole so he could decide who he was obligated to love and who he could ignore. Jesus answered by redefining the question: don't ask 'Who is my neighbor?'; ask 'Am I BEING a neighbor?' Look at the religious leaders: the priest and the Levite were professional clergy on their way from temple service. They saw the beaten, bloody man and crossed the street! They had correct theology, but zero compassion. But the Samaritan—an outsider despised as a religious heretic—was moved with deep compassion. Early church fathers saw here the Gospel: we are the dying traveler, stripped and beaten by sin and Satan; religion and the Law passed by powerless to save us. But Jesus, despised and rejected of men, came where we were, poured in the oil of the Spirit and the wine of His blood, carried us into the inn of His Church, and paid the full price for our restoration! Go and do likewise.

lessons.lesson: Orthodoxy Without Compassion Is Dead
lessons.detail: The priest and Levite had flawless ceremonial credentials, but their religious busyness blinded them to suffering human need.
lessons.question: Does your religious routine ever cause you to pass by people who are hurting, lonely, or broken?

lessons.lesson: Compassion Crosses Every Prejudiced Boundary
lessons.detail: Jews and Samaritans despised each other, yet this traveler saw beyond race, politics, and religion to bandage a fellow human being.
lessons.question: Are there people of different backgrounds, lifestyles, or opinions whom God is calling you to show practical mercy to?

lessons.lesson: Love Costs Time, Energy, and Money
lessons.detail: The Samaritan gave his wine, his oil, his donkey, his afternoon, and two days of wages to nurse an enemy back to health.
lessons.question: Does your love for others cost you personal convenience and real financial sacrifice?

lessons.lesson: Don't Withhold Good When It Is in Your Power
lessons.detail: Never tell a suffering neighbor to come back tomorrow when you have the capacity to relieve their pain today.
lessons.question: Is there a practical act of kindness or generosity that you have been delaying that you should do right now?

264.notesPrompt: Reflect on Jesus' command: 'Go and do likewise.' Who is the 'beaten traveler' on the roadside of your everyday routine? What practical step of mercy can you take for them this week?

quiz.question: What question did the lawyer ask to justify himself in Luke 10:29?
options: When will the kingdom of God come?
Why do your disciples eat on the Sabbath?
quiz.explanation: Luke 10:29 states: 'But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”'

quiz.question: What two religious figures saw the beaten traveler and passed by on the other side?
options: A Roman centurion and a tax collector
quiz.explanation: A priest was going down that way and passed by on the other side; likewise a Levite came, saw him, and passed by on the other side.

quiz.question: What two substances did the Samaritan pour into the traveler's wounds in Luke 10:34?
quiz.explanation: He came to him, and bound up his wounds, 'pouring on oil and wine.'

quiz.question: How much money did the Samaritan leave with the innkeeper for the wounded man's care?
options: Two denarii (approx. two days' wages), with a promise to repay any extra upon return
Nothing, he promised to pay later
quiz.explanation: He took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said: 'Take care of him. Whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I return.'

quiz.question: True or False: According to Proverbs 3:27, we should withhold good from the needy whenever we feel tired.
quiz.explanation: False. Proverbs 3:27 commands: 'Don't withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus Christ, You are the true Good Samaritan who descended into our beaten, broken world when religion and human systems passed us by on the other side. You were moved with compassion; You poured the oil of Your Spirit and the wine of Your blood into our wounds, bore our griefs on Your own shoulders, and paid the full ransom for our eternal restoration! Forgive me for the times I have crossed to the other side to avoid the inconvenience of messy human suffering. Give me Your eyes of compassion. Teach me to bind up the broken, love across every barrier, and go and do likewise in Your holy name.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: He who showed mercy is the true neighbor; Lord Jesus, grant me Your compassionate heart to go and do likewise.
closingPrayer.prompt: Look for an opportunity today to show practical mercy (giving, bandaging, helping, listening) to someone who cannot repay you.

265.character: The Prodigal Son & The Elder Brother
265.season: The Running Father: Extravagant Grace for Runaways and Legalists
265.theme: The extravagant grace of the Father welcomes the repentant runaway home with open arms and joyful feast.

memoryVerse.text: “He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: God does not wait coldly with folded arms for repentant sinners to grovel; our heavenly Father runs out to meet us, wraps us in His robe of grace, and throws a celebration.

cramData.firstLetters: “H a, a c t h f. B w h w s f o, h f s h, a w m w c, a r, a f o h n, a k h.”

profile.title: The Parable of the Father and Two Sons: The Extravagant Love of God
profile.who: In response to Pharisees grumbling that Jesus welcomes sinners and eats with them, Jesus told the crown jewel of His parables: a younger son who demanded his inheritance, wasted it in reckless living in a distant country, and returned home to become a hired servant; only to be met by a running father who restored him with a robe, ring, sandals, and the fattened calf; contrasting with an angry, legalistic older brother who refused to celebrate.
profile.whenAndWhere: The road through Perea toward Jerusalem, circa AD 29.
profile.family: A wealthy father with two sons: the younger rebellious runaway and the older bitter moralist.
keyMoments: The younger son asked his father for his share of the estate (tantamount to wishing his father dead); the father divided his livelihood between them.
Traveled into a far country, wasted his substance in wild living, ran out of money just as a severe famine struck, and ended up feeding pigs—the ultimate humiliation for a Jew.
Longed to fill his stomach with the carob pods the swine ate, but no one gave him anything.

Came to his senses: 'How many of my father's hired servants have bread enough to spare, and I'm dying with hunger! I will get up and go to my father, and tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight. I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”'

He arose and came to his father; but while he was still a long way off, his father saw him, was moved with compassion, pulled up his robes, RAN (breaking Middle Eastern patriarchal dignity), fell on his neck, and kissed him repeatedly.

The son began his rehearsed confession, but the father interrupted: 'Bring out the best robe, and put it on him! Put a ring on his finger, and sandals on his feet! Bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let's eat and celebrate; for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found!'
The older brother returned from the field, heard music and dancing, was furious, and refused to go inside.

The father came outside and pleaded with him; the older son raged: 'These many years I have served you and never disobeyed your command, yet you never gave me a young goat to celebrate with my friends; but when this son of yours came who devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him!'

The father answered with infinite gentleness: 'Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours. But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.'
strengths: The younger son's honest repentance: came to his senses and returned home.
The father's boundless, extravagant grace: ran, embraced, restored, and celebrated.
The father's patient love for the self-righteous older brother.
failures: The younger son's selfish hedonism and squandering of his father's inheritance.
The older son's cold legalism, loveless bitterness, and refusal to rejoice over his brother's restoration.

scripture.title: The Parable of the Prodigal Son and the Waiting Father

verses.text: “When he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough to spare, and I'm dying with hunger!’”
“‘I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.”’”
“He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.”
“But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and sandals on his feet.’”
“‘for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ They began to celebrate.”
“He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.’”
“‘But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”

scripture.title: The Spirit of Adoption and Unfailing Love

verses.text: For you didn't receive the spirit of bondservants again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;
For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: The Father Runs to Meet You: Grace Restores You from the Pigpen to the Banquet
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Look at the posture of the father in Luke 15:20. In the ancient Near East, an elderly patriarch never ran; running required gathering up his long tunics, exposing his bare legs, which was considered deeply undignified. Why did the father run? In Jewish culture, if a boy lost his Jewish inheritance among the Gentiles, the village elders would gather at the city gate to perform the 'Qetsatsah' ceremony—breaking a clay pot at his feet to declare him permanently cut off from his community! The father ran so he could reach his broken boy before the village elders could shame him! The father absorbed the humiliation and wrapped him in a protective embrace! Before the boy could even finish his speech about becoming a hired hand, the father cut him off: 'Bring out the BEST robe (Christ's righteousness)! Put a ring on his finger (family authority)! Put sandals on his feet (slaves went barefoot, sons wore shoes)! Kill the fattened calf!' God does not tolerate you as a servant; He celebrates you as a beloved child.

lessons.lesson: Sin Always Promises Freedom and Delivers a Pigpen
lessons.detail: The far country of rebellion looked glamorous at first, but ended in bankruptcy, spiritual starvation, and feeding unclean swine.
lessons.question: Is there a worldly allure in your life that is promising fulfillment but secretly dragging you into spiritual starvation?

lessons.lesson: Repentance Begins When You 'Come to Yourself'
lessons.detail: True repentance is returning to spiritual sanity: recognizing the Father's overflowing goodness and walking home with honest confession.
lessons.question: What is keeping you from arising right now and walking straight back into your heavenly Father's open arms?

lessons.lesson: The Father's Grace Outruns Our Guilt
lessons.detail: While the son was still far off, the father ran, kissed him, and covered his filthy rags with the best robe of honor.
lessons.question: Do you view God as an angry warden waiting to punish you, or as a loving Father running to welcome you home?

lessons.lesson: Beware of the Bitter Heart of the Older Brother
lessons.detail: The older brother stayed in the house but was just as lost in his self-righteous, loveless legalism as the younger brother was in the pigpen.
lessons.question: Are you harboring self-righteous resentment toward someone who has lived a messy life and received God's lavish grace?

265.notesPrompt: Reflect on Luke 15:20: 'While he was still far off, his father saw him, was moved with compassion, ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.' Write a letter of praise to your Father for the day He ran out to meet you.

quiz.question: Where did the younger son end up working when famine struck the far country in Luke 15:14-15?
options: Feeding pigs in the fields, longing to eat the carob pods the swine ate
At the customs office in Caesarea
quiz.explanation: He was sent into the fields to feed pigs, longing to fill his belly with the pods the swine ate.

options: He was moved with compassion, ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him

quiz.explanation: While he was still far off, his father saw him, was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

options: A sword, a shield, and a helmet

options: He resented that his father celebrated the return of the prodigal who squandered his estate, while never giving him a goat to feast with friends

quiz.explanation: The older son was bitter because he felt his years of strict obedience went unrewarded while the wasteful brother received the fattened calf.

quiz.question: True or False: According to Romans 8:38-39, trials, death, or any created thing can easily separate us from the love of God in Christ.
quiz.explanation: False. Paul is persuaded that nothing in all creation will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Abba, Heavenly Father, what extravagant, unbelievable love You have demonstrated to my soul! When I wandered into the far country of self-will, squandering Your blessings and wallowing in the pigpens of sin, You never stopped watching the horizon for my return. Thank You that when I came to myself and took one trembling step toward home, You pulled up Your robes and RAN to meet me! You kissed my neck, stripped away my filthy rags, and clothed me in the best robe of Jesus' righteousness. Cleanse my heart from the bitter legalism of the older brother. Let me rejoice with all of heaven whenever a lost child is found and brought home to Your banquet table.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Abba Father, You ran to meet me and restored me with Your kiss of grace; I rejoice in Your unfailing love.
closingPrayer.prompt: If you have felt distant from God, picture your Father running toward you right now with open arms; whisper a simple prayer returning home.

266.season: Where Are the Nine? Returning to Give Glory at His Feet
266.theme: True gratitude returns to the feet of Jesus, receiving not just physical healing but complete spiritual wholeness.

memoryVerse.text: “Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: All ten lepers had the faith to cry for mercy and obey the command to go to the priest, but only one returned to fall on his face in worship, receiving spiritual wholeness through gratitude.

cramData.firstLetters: “W t n f w r t g g t G, e t s?”

profile.title: The Grateful Samaritan Leper: The One Who Returned to Worship
profile.who: One of ten lepers living in an ostracized colony along the border between Samaria and Galilee; all ten cried for mercy and were cleansed as they walked to show themselves to the priests, but this solitary Samaritan foreigner turned back immediately, praising God with a loud voice and falling on his face at Jesus' feet in exuberant thanksgiving.
profile.whenAndWhere: A village along the border of Samaria and Galilee, circa AD 29.
profile.family: A Samaritan stranger (allogenes—foreigner); outcast from both Jewish and Samaritan communities due to leprosy.
keyMoments: Ten men who were lepers stood afar off, adhering to quarantine laws, and lifted up their voices crying: 'Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!'
Jesus saw them and gave a test of obedience: 'Go and show yourselves to the priests' (who alone had authority to pronounce a leper clean under Leviticus 14).
As they went, walking in obedience before seeing physical evidence, they were all cleansed—their decaying skin restored to healthy flesh.
Nine of the men kept running forward, eager to receive official certificates of health, re-enter society, and resume their lives.
One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back immediately, glorifying God with a loud voice.
Fell on his face at Jesus' feet, giving Him profuse, heartfelt thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
Jesus asked the piercing questions that ring through history: 'Weren't the ten cleansed? But where are the nine? Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?'

Jesus said to the prostrate worshiper: 'Arise, and go your way. Your faith has made you well (sesoken se—has saved you / made you whole).' The nine received physical cleansing; the grateful Samaritan received eternal spiritual salvation.
strengths: Valued the Giver above the gift: stopped everything to return to the feet of Jesus.
Unashamed, vocal worship: glorified God with a loud voice.
Extravagant gratitude: fell flat on his face before Christ.
failures: Had lived in the terrible physical and social decay of leprosy.

scripture.title: The Ten Cleansed Lepers and the One Who Returned

verses.text: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
He fell on his face at Jesus' feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered, “Weren't the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?”
“Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?”
He said to him, “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”

scripture.title: Bless Yahweh and Forget Not All His Benefits

verses.text: Praise Yahweh, my soul! All that is within me, praise his holy name!
Praise Yahweh, my soul, and don't forget all his benefits;
who forgives all your sins; who heals all your diseases;
who redeems your life from destruction; who crowns you with loving kindness and tender mercies;

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Ten Received the Gift, but Only One Received the Giver: The Power of Thankfulness
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Notice the tragic statistic in this story: a 90 percent ingratitude rate among people who had experienced a life-transforming miracle! All ten cried for mercy; all ten obeyed Jesus' command to go to the priests; all ten experienced the miraculous cleansing of their flesh. But nine of them were so obsessed with the blessing that they forgot the Blesser! They took their restored skin and ran straight into normal life without a backward glance toward the Savior. Only one man—a despised Samaritan outsider—stopped dead in his tracks. He realized that the priest in the temple had nothing compared to the Prophet on the road! He ran back shouting praises and threw himself flat at the feet of Jesus. And Jesus gave him something the other nine never received: 'Your faith has made you whole (saved you).' Ingratitude is satisfied with physical relief; gratitude falls in love with the Savior and receives eternal life.

lessons.lesson: Don't Fall in Love with the Gift and Forget the Giver
lessons.detail: It is easy to seek God frantically during a crisis, and then completely neglect Him once health, finances, or relief arrives.
lessons.question: Are you as passionate about thanking Jesus for answered prayers as you were about begging Him for help?

lessons.lesson: Obedience Precedes the Physical Miracle
lessons.detail: They were cleansed 'as they went'; step out in faith on God's Word even before you see the physical evidence of the breakthrough.
lessons.question: What step of obedience is God calling you to take in faith before the answer visibly appears?

lessons.lesson: Gratitude Elevates Physical Healing to Spiritual Wholeness
lessons.detail: The nine received clean skin, but the tenth man received salvation of his soul because his gratitude brought him to Jesus' feet.
lessons.question: How does intentional daily thanksgiving deepen your spiritual intimacy with Christ?

lessons.lesson: Forget Not All His Benefits
lessons.detail: Like David in Psalm 103, actively command your soul to remember God's forgiveness, healing, redemption, and lovingkindness.
lessons.question: What specific benefits and mercies of God have you experienced recently that you need to thank Him for today?

266.notesPrompt: List ten specific blessings, answers to prayer, or mercies God has given you this week. Spend intentional time falling at His feet in verbal praise, refusing to be like the nine.

quiz.question: How many lepers met Jesus and cried 'Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!' in Luke 17:12-13?
quiz.explanation: Luke 17:12-13 states that ten men who were lepers met Him, stood at a distance, and cried for mercy.

quiz.question: At what point were the ten lepers cleansed of their disease in Luke 17:14?
options: Immediately when Jesus touched their foreheads
As they went to show themselves to the priests
After washing seven times in the Jordan
quiz.explanation: Luke 17:14 records: 'As they went, they were cleansed.'

quiz.question: How many of the ten cleansed lepers returned to thank Jesus in Luke 17:15?
options: Only one of them, and he was a Samaritan
quiz.explanation: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice and fell on his face at Jesus' feet, giving thanks; and he was a Samaritan.

quiz.question: What question did Jesus ask when the solitary Samaritan fell at His feet in Luke 17:17-18?
options: Why did you leave the priests?
Weren't the ten cleansed? But where are the nine? Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?
How much money do you have?
quiz.explanation: Jesus asked: 'Weren't the ten cleansed? But where are the nine? Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?'

quiz.question: True or False: According to Psalm 103:2, we are encouraged to forget God's past benefits so we can focus on new ones.
quiz.explanation: False. Psalm 103:2 commands: 'Praise Yahweh, my soul, and don't forget all his benefits.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Great Physician and Merciful High Priest, I return to Your feet today with a loud voice of thanksgiving! Forgive me for the countless times I have been like the ungrateful nine: eager to beg for Your help in distress, but quick to run away with Your blessings without falling on my face in gratitude. Praise Yahweh, my soul, and forget not all His benefits! You have forgiven all my iniquities; You have redeemed my life from destruction; You have crowned me with lovingkindness. I worship at Your feet today, Lord Jesus, declaring that You are worthy of all my praise.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God? Lord Jesus, I return to Your feet with exuberant thanksgiving.
closingPrayer.prompt: Call or message someone today specifically to say 'thank you' for a blessing or kindness they showed you in the past.

267.season: One Thing You Lack: What Does It Profit to Keep the World?
267.theme: Jesus demands undivided allegiance, loving us enough to expose the earthly treasures that hold us hostage.

memoryVerse.text: Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Jesus loves us too deeply to let us keep idols that destroy our souls; true discipleship requires loosening our grip on earthly wealth to embrace treasure in heaven.

cramData.firstLetters: J l a h l h, a s t h, “O t y l. G, s w y h, a g t t p, a y w h t i h; a c, f m, t u t c.”

profile.title: The Rich Young Ruler: The Moral Seeker Who Walked Away Sorrowful
profile.who: An aristocratic young Jewish magistrate (ruler of a local synagogue or civil court) of immense wealth and impeccable outward morality who ran to Jesus, kneeled in the dust, and asked how to inherit eternal life; when Jesus looked upon him with deep love and demanded that he surrender his wealth to the poor to follow Him, the young man's face fell and he departed grieving because his wealth possessed him.
profile.whenAndWhere: Perea on the road toward Jerusalem, circa AD 30.
profile.family: A wealthy young ruler of the Jewish nobility.
keyMoments: Ran to Jesus as He went out into the way, kneeled down before Him in the road, and asked: 'Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?'

Jesus challenged his standard of goodness: 'Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God. You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, honor your father and mother.'
The young man answered with confident sincerity: 'Teacher, all these things I have observed from my youth.'
Mark records an unforgettable detail in Mark 10:21: 'Jesus looking at him LOVED him.' Jesus saw his moral earnestness and looked upon him with genuine affection.

Put His divine finger on the one idol holding his heart hostage: 'One thing you lack: go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.'
At that saying, the young man's face fell, his countenance grew dark with sorrow, and he walked away grieving; for he was one who had great possessions.

Jesus looked around and remarked to His disciples: 'How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into the Kingdom of God! It is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter into God's Kingdom.'
Disciples were astonished: 'Then who can be saved?' Jesus answered: 'With men it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.'
strengths: Eager, humble approach: ran and kneeled in the dust before an itinerant Rabbi despite his aristocratic rank.
Moral earnestness: kept the outward commandments from youth.
Recognized that despite wealth and religion, he still lacked eternal life.
failures: Possessed by his possessions: loved his earthly wealth more than the Son of God, choosing money over discipleship.

scripture.title: The Rich Young Ruler and the Needle's Eye

verses.text: As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, kneeled before him, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.”

Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
But his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.
Jesus looked around, and said to his disciples, “How difficult it will be for those who have riches to enter into God's Kingdom!”
Jesus, looking at them, said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”

scripture.title: A Ruler Asks About Inheriting Eternal Life

verses.text: A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
When Jesus heard these things, he said to him, “You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have, and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Come, follow me.”
When he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.
He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, for the Kingdom of God's sake,”
“who will not receive manifold more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.”

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Jesus Loves You Too Much to Settle for Second Place in Your Heart
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Notice the heart of Jesus in Mark 10:21: 'Jesus, looking at him, LOVED him.' Jesus did not give this man a harsh command because He hated him; He gave it because He loved him! Jesus saw that this young man was held hostage by his bank account. He thought he possessed his riches, but his riches possessed him! He had kept the commandments of the second tablet (not murdering, stealing, or lying), but he was completely violating the First Commandment: 'You shall have no other gods before Me!' His money was his god. When Jesus told him to sell his possessions and give to the poor, Jesus was offering him the trade of a lifetime: trade perishable dust for eternal treasure in heaven, and walk with the Son of God! But the young man looked at his silver, looked at Jesus, bowed his head, and walked away sorrowful. What is the 'one thing' holding your heart hostage today? Let it go; Jesus is worth infinitely more.

lessons.lesson: External Morality Does Not Equal Salvation
lessons.detail: The young man lived a clean, religious life, yet Jesus said, 'One thing you lack.' Good behavior cannot substitute for total surrender to Christ.
lessons.question: Are you relying on your moral track record, or have you surrendered everything to follow Jesus?

lessons.lesson: Jesus Loves Us Enough to Expose Our Idols
lessons.detail: True divine love does not pamper our spiritual addictions; it points straight to the idol that threatens to drag our soul to hell.
lessons.question: What is the primary idol or attachment that the Holy Spirit is asking you to loosen your grip on?

lessons.lesson: Possessions Can Possess the Soul
lessons.detail: The young man walked away grieving because his wealth owned him; we must hold all earthly goods with an open, surrendered hand.
lessons.question: Do you own your possessions, or do your possessions, savings, and comforts own you?

lessons.lesson: What Is Impossible with Man Is Possible with God
lessons.detail: Human hearts cannot untangle themselves from greed by mere willpower, but God's supernatural grace can deliver any soul.
lessons.question: Are you asking God to do the impossible in freeing your heart from materialism and worldly anxiety?

267.notesPrompt: Reflect on Mark 10:21: 'One thing you lack... come, follow me, taking up the cross.' What is the 'one thing' between you and total, wholehearted discipleship to Jesus?

quiz.question: True or False: According to Mark 10:27, salvation for wealthy people is utterly impossible, even for God.
quiz.explanation: False. Jesus declared: 'With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus Christ, You looked upon the rich young ruler with infinite love, and You look upon my soul today with that same penetrating love. You know the idols that compete for my allegiance. You know the earthly treasures, bank accounts, comforts, and reputations that I am tempted to cling to. Forgive me for the times I have held back from total discipleship out of fear of loss. Today I open my hands: all that I have belongs to You. Deliver me from being possessed by my possessions. I exchange the passing dust of this world for eternal treasure in heaven. I take up my cross to follow You, my Lord and my All.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: Search my heart, Lord Jesus; expose the one thing I lack, and grant me grace to surrender all to follow You.
closingPrayer.prompt: Identify one material item or financial security you have held tightly, and mentally surrender it to Jesus with open hands.

268.season: The Sycamore Tree of Jericho: Salvation Has Come to This House
268.theme: The relentless seeking love of the Son of Man transforms greedy hearts into joyful fountains of restitution.

memoryVerse.text: “For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: We do not find God; the Son of Man seeks us out in our brokenness, stopping beneath our sycamore trees to bring joyful salvation into our homes.

cramData.firstLetters: “F t S o M c t s a t s t w w l.”

profile.title: Zacchaeus of Jericho: The Chief Tax Collector Who Climbed into Grace
profile.who: The wealthy chief tax collector (architelones) in the affluent winter resort city of Jericho, hated as a collaborator with Rome and an extortioner; short of stature, he climbed a sycamore fig tree to see Jesus passing by; Jesus looked up, called him by name, invited Himself to his house, and transformed his life into radical generosity and fourfold restitution.
profile.whenAndWhere: Jericho, in the Jordan Valley, circa AD 30 (days before the crucifixion).
profile.family: A Jewish son of Abraham, head of a household in Jericho.
keyMoments: Jesus entered and was passing through the wealthy oasis city of Jericho on His final journey toward Jerusalem.
A man named Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector (supervising regional tax collectors in a major customs hub) and was very rich.
Desperately wanted to see who Jesus was, but couldn't because of the thick crowd, since he was small in stature.
Ran on ahead, abandoning all dignity of a senior civil official, and climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree to see Him, for He was to pass that way.
When Jesus reached the spot, He looked up, saw him, and called him by name: 'Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house!'
Hurried and came down, and received Jesus into his home joyfully.
The religious crowd grumbled in self-righteous disgust: 'He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner!'

Standing before the Lord, Zacchaeus demonstrated radical, instant transformation of heart: 'Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much!' (Going far beyond Mosaic law requirements).
Jesus declared: 'Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham!'
Spoke His supreme mission statement in Luke 19:10: 'For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.'
Fulfilled Ezekiel 18:21, 27: 'If the wicked turns from all his sins... he will surely live; he will not die.'
strengths: Overcame social embarrassment and physical limitations to see Jesus.
Welcomed Jesus into his home with exuberant joy.
Radical, voluntary repentance evidenced by immense financial restitution (fourfold) and generosity (half his wealth to the poor).
failures: Grew wealthy through years of unjust taxation and extortion as chief of publicans.

scripture.title: Jesus and Zacchaeus in Jericho

verses.text: Behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn't because of the crowd, because he was short.
He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was to pass that way.
When Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.
Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”
Jesus said to him, “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.”
“For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

scripture.title: Repentance, Restitution, and Turning from Iniquity

verses.text: “But if the wicked turns away from all his sins that he has committed, and keeps all my statutes, and does that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live. He shall not die.”
“None of his transgressions that he has committed will be remembered against him. In his righteousness that he has done, he shall live.”
“Again, when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness that he has committed, and does that which is lawful and right, he will save his soul alive.”

whatGodIsSaying.headline: The Seeking Savior Calls You by Name and Transforms Your Pocketbook with Joy
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Zacchaeus thought he was the one seeking Jesus; but when he climbed that sycamore tree, he discovered that Jesus had been seeking HIM all along! Jesus stopped directly beneath the branches, looked up into the foliage, and called him by his personal name: 'Zacchaeus, hurry and come down; today I MUST stay at your house!' Jesus did not wait for Zacchaeus to apologize before offering friendship. Grace always takes the initiative! And notice how true salvation showed up in Zacchaeus' life: it immediately touched his wallet! Zacchaeus did not wait to be sued or audited; standing before the love of Jesus, his greedy heart melted into a fountain of generosity: 'Half my goods I give to the poor, and fourfold restitution to anyone I defrauded!' When the grace of Christ enters a house, greed dies, restitution is made, and joy floods the home. The Son of Man came to seek and save that which was lost—and that includes you.

lessons.lesson: Don't Let Dignity Keep You from Jesus
lessons.detail: A wealthy chief official climbed a tree like a boy because seeing Jesus was more important than preserving his social dignity.
lessons.question: Are you willing to set aside your pride, image, and reputation in order to pursue Jesus wholeheartedly?

lessons.lesson: Jesus Knows Your Name and Stops at Your Tree
lessons.detail: Jesus did not know Zacchaeus through an introduction; the Shepherd knows every lost sheep by name and seeks them out.
lessons.question: Do you realize that Jesus sees you right where you are, knows your name, and desires intimate fellowship in your home?

lessons.lesson: True Repentance Makes Tangible Restitution
lessons.detail: Zacchaeus proved his conversion not with empty tears, but by paying back fourfold to those he had wronged and blessing the poor.
lessons.question: Is there someone you have wronged financially or relationally to whom you need to make humble restitution?

lessons.lesson: The Mission of Jesus: Seeking the Lost
lessons.detail: The entire purpose of the Incarnation is summarized here: the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.
lessons.question: Does your life mission align with Christ's mission to seek and rescue lost, hurting people around you?

268.notesPrompt: Reflect on Luke 19:10: 'The Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.' Write a prayer of thanksgiving for how Jesus sought you out when you were lost in your own sycamore tree.

options: A chief tax collector, and he was rich

options: He was hiding from Roman soldiers

options: Woe to you, extortioner of Jericho!

options: He gave one tenth of his crop
