Never underestimate the power of an ordinary, obedient believer who is willing to welcome an enemy as a brother.

lessons.lesson: It is safe to voice your honest fears to God in prayer, as long as you remain willing to obey.
lessons.detail: Ananias voiced his realistic dread of Saul, and Jesus met his doubts with reassurance and clear divine purpose.
lessons.question: Do you express your honest fears to the Lord when He calls you into uncomfortable or intimidating obedience?

lessons.lesson: God sees what broken people will become by His grace, not merely what they were in their past.
lessons.detail: Ananias saw a dangerous terrorist; Jesus saw a 'chosen vessel' who would carry His name before emperors and kings.
lessons.question: Are you judging difficult people by their past sins, or seeing them through the eyes of Christ's transforming grace?

lessons.lesson: Overcoming evil with good begins with extending the greeting of reconciliation.
lessons.detail: By calling him 'Brother Saul,' Ananias practiced Romans 12:21 before it was ever penned, welcoming an enemy into the family of God.
lessons.question: Is there someone who has opposed or offended you whom you need to address with words of grace and brotherhood?

lessons.lesson: Quiet, unseen obedience often plays a pivotal role in unleashing global spiritual impact.
lessons.detail: We hear almost nothing else about Ananias in Scripture, yet his willingness to lay hands on Saul changed the course of world history.
lessons.question: Are you content to play a small, unseen part in God's Kingdom, trusting Him for the eternal harvest?

quiz.question: On what specific street in Damascus was Ananias instructed to find Saul?
quiz.explanation: Acts 9:11 notes: 'Arise, and go to the street which is called Straight...'

quiz.question: What activity did the Lord tell Ananias that Saul was currently doing?
quiz.explanation: The Lord told Ananias: 'For behold, he is praying...'

quiz.question: What revolutionary two-word greeting did Ananias use when he laid hands on Saul?
quiz.explanation: Acts 9:17 records: 'Laying his hands on him, he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord... has sent me...”'

quiz.question: Ananias refused to go to Saul and was struck with leprosy for his disobedience.
quiz.explanation: False. Ananias departed, entered the house, laid hands on Saul, and baptized him.

quiz.question: What physical manifestation happened to Saul's eyes when Ananias laid hands on him?
options: Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight
He remained blind for ten more years
quiz.explanation: Acts 9:18 states: 'Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus, I marvel at the quiet, courageous obedience of Ananias. When You call me to step out of my comfort zone and minister to people who intimidate, offend, or frighten me, deliver me from paralyzed hesitation. Give me eyes to see people as You see them—not as ruined sinners, but as chosen vessels waiting for Your redeeming touch. Put the words 'Brother' and 'Sister' upon my lips. Help me to overcome evil with good, to bless those who persecute, and to be a faithful conduit of Your Holy Spirit to bring sight, healing, and baptism to searching souls.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “Go your way; for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings...”
closingPrayer.prompt: Ask God for grace to extend a hand of genuine Christian fellowship to someone you have previously avoided.

302.season: Joppa: The Needle, the Tunics, and Practical Mercy
302.theme: Quiet acts of practical mercy weave garments of love that touch the heart of God and community.

memoryVerse.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Christian faith is validated not by loud sermons, but by tangible acts of compassionate love; Dorcas preached the Gospel through her needle and thread, clothing destitute widows and leaving a fragrance of Christ that outlived her death.

cramData.firstLetters: N t w a J a c d n T, w w t, m D. T w w f o g w a a o m w s d.

profile.title: Tabitha (Dorcas) of Joppa: The Disciple Whose Needle Preached the Gospel
profile.who: A beloved female disciple living in the Mediterranean port city of Joppa, known in Aramaic as Tabitha and Greek as Dorcas ('Gazelle'); renowned for being 'full of good works and almsdeeds,' she spent her life sewing tunics and coats for impoverished widows; when she fell sick and died, the weeping widows sent for Peter, who knelt in prayer and raised her from the dead.
profile.whenAndWhere: Joppa (modern Jaffa/Tel Aviv), on the Mediterranean coast of Judea, circa AD 36.
profile.family: A single or widowed Christian woman; spiritual mother to Joppa's widows.
keyMoments: Spending her days quietly cutting cloth and sewing warm tunics and garments for destitute widows.
Falling critically ill and dying, causing grief to shatter the entire local Christian community.
Being washed and laid in an upper room as believers dispatched two messengers to summon Peter from nearby Lydda.
Peter arriving to find the room crowded with weeping widows proudly showing him the hand-sewn garments Dorcas had made for them.
Peter putting everyone outside, kneeling down in prayer, and saying: 'Tabitha, arise!'—watching her open her eyes, sit up, and presenting her alive to the astonished saints.
profile.strengths: Radical servant-hearted generosity, tireless practical compassion, deeply loved by the poor, pure living faith.
profile.failures: None recorded in Scripture; held up as an exemplar of practical Christian charity.

scripture.title: Tabitha's Life of Mercy and Her Resurrection

verses.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.
In those days, she became sick, and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.
As Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to them.

Peter arose and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made while she was with them.
Peter put them all out, and kneeled down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, arise!” She opened her eyes; and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
He gave her his hand, and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
It became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

scripture.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead

verses.text: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can that faith save him?
If a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,
and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” and yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?
Even so faith, if it has no works is dead in itself.
Yes, a man will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Heaven notices and treasures the quiet stitches of love you weave into broken lives; genuine faith clothes the naked with Christlike mercy.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Notice how Luke introduces this precious woman in Acts 9:36: she is called a *mathetria*—the only time the feminine form of 'disciple' appears in the entire New Testament! What made Dorcas a master disciple? She never wrote an epistle; she never preached a sermon recorded in the book of Acts; she never debated theologians in the Sanhedrin. Dorcas held a needle and thread. In first-century society, widows were the most vulnerable, impoverished people in the world—destitute, without pensions or welfare, often shivering in the damp Mediterranean winters. Dorcas didn't just pray for them and say, 'Be warmed and filled' (James 2:16); she bought fabric, measured their shoulders, and hand-stitched warm coats and tunics! When she died, the widows didn't just weep—they held up the coats! They showed Peter the tangible evidence of her faith. Her legacy was written not on parchment, but in the warm fabric covering the backs of the poor. And when Peter knelt and commanded, 'Tabitha, arise!' God honored her practical, hidden devotion by restoring her breath, sparking a massive revival where 'many believed in the Lord.' Your small acts of kindness are never wasted in God's eyes.

lessons.lesson: True Christian discipleship is revealed through tangible acts of mercy, not empty words.
lessons.detail: Dorcas was 'full of good works and acts of mercy'; authentic faith puts practical shoes on compassion by meeting physical needs.
lessons.question: What practical service are you currently doing that directly alleviates the suffering of someone in need?

lessons.lesson: God can take the simplest everyday skill—like sewing—and use it as an altar of kingdom ministry.
lessons.detail: You do not need a public pulpit to glorify Christ; whatever talent or craft you possess can become an instrument of Gospel love.
lessons.question: What hobby, trade, or domestic skill do you have that could be used to bless the hurting and poor?

lessons.lesson: The love you sow into the lives of the needy will be your greatest memorial before God and men.
lessons.detail: The weeping widows holding up Dorcas' handmade garments was the most eloquent funeral tribute ever paid to a follower of Christ.
lessons.question: When your earthly life is finished, what tangible evidence of sacrificial love will people remember?

lessons.lesson: God delights in honoring and restoring those who pour out their lives for the defenseless.
lessons.detail: God raised Dorcas from the dead, demonstrating that heaven values the servant who washes the feet and clothes the bodies of the vulnerable.
lessons.question: Does knowing that God notices your unseen acts of kindness motivate you to persist when unappreciated?

quiz.question: What does the name Tabitha mean when translated into Greek?
quiz.explanation: Acts 9:36 states: 'named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas' (meaning a gazelle).

quiz.question: In what Mediterranean coastal town did Tabitha live and serve?
quiz.explanation: Scripture explicitly specifies: 'Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha...'

quiz.question: What did the weeping widows show Peter when he arrived in the upper room?
options: The coats and garments which Dorcas made while she was with them
A deed of land in Galilee
quiz.explanation: Acts 9:39 notes: 'showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made while she was with them.'

quiz.question: Peter commanded everyone to leave the room, kneeled down, prayed, and said: 'Tabitha, arise!'
quiz.explanation: True. Peter put them all out, kneeled down, prayed, and said: 'Tabitha, arise!' and she opened her eyes.

quiz.question: According to James 2:17, what is faith if it does not have works?
quiz.explanation: James writes: 'Even so faith, if it has no works is dead in itself.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus, You were rich, yet for our sakes You became poor, clothing our naked souls in the white robe of Your righteousness. Thank You for the quiet, radiant testimony of Tabitha. Forgive me for pursuing flashy, visible spiritual achievements while ignoring the physical, practical needs of the hungry and naked around me. Take the needle, the tools, the resources, and the skills in my hands, Lord. Fill me with genuine acts of mercy and good works. Let my faith be alive, active, and tenderly affectionate to the forgotten and broken, bringing many in my community to believe in Your holy name.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.
closingPrayer.prompt: Identify one practical physical need in your church or neighborhood: commit to meeting it with Christlike generosity this week.

303.season: Caesarea: The Roman Centurion and the Gentile Pentecost
303.theme: God tears down religious barriers and pours out His Spirit on Gentiles who hunger for His truth.

memoryVerse.text: Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism; but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: The Gospel has no ethnic or national boundaries; God does not play favorites, but welcomes all people everywhere who fear Him and receive the cleansing blood of Jesus Christ.

cramData.firstLetters: P o h m a s, “T I p t G d s f; b i e n h w f h a w r i a t h.”

profile.title: Cornelius the Roman Centurion: The First Gentile Convert of the Church
profile.who: A Roman centurion of the Italian Cohort stationed in Caesarea Maritima, a devout God-fearing Gentile who prayed continually and gave generously to the Jewish poor; directed by an angel in a vision to send for Peter in Joppa, his household heard the Gospel and experienced the 'Gentile Pentecost' as the Holy Spirit fell upon them while Peter was still speaking.
profile.whenAndWhere: The Roman garrison city of Caesarea Maritima, Judea, circa AD 38–40.
profile.family: Roman military commander; head of a devout, God-fearing household.
keyMoments: Praying at the ninth hour (3 PM) and seeing an angel who told him: 'Your prayers and your gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before God.'
Sending loyal soldiers to Joppa to invite Simon Peter to his home.
Gathering his family, relatives, and close friends to listen with hungry hearts to whatever God commanded Peter to speak.
Hearing Peter proclaim Christ's life, death, resurrection, and the forgiveness of sins through His name.
Being overwhelmed by the Holy Spirit falling upon all the Gentiles, speaking in tongues and glorifying God, and being baptized in water.
profile.strengths: Deep reverence for God, disciplined prayer life, generous giving, humble teachability before God's Word.
profile.failures: Initially fell down at Peter's feet to worship him, which Peter quickly corrected: 'Stand up! I myself am also a man.'

scripture.title: The Vision of Peter and the Gentile Pentecost at Caesarea

verses.text: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,
a devout man, and one who feared God with all his house, who gave gifts for the needy generously to the people, and always prayed to God.
“Therefore I sent to you at once, and it was good of you to come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of God to hear all things that have been commanded you by the Lord.”
Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism;
but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.
All the prophets testify about him, that through his name, everyone who believes in him will receive remission of sins.”
While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those who heard the word.
They of the circumcision who believed were amazed, as many as came with Peter, because the gift of the Holy Spirit was also poured out on the Gentiles.
For they heard them speak with other languages and magnify God. Then Peter answered,
“Can anyone forbid these people from being baptized with water, who have received the Holy Spirit as well as we?”

scripture.title: God Grants Repentance Unto Life to the Gentiles

verses.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.
I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, ‘John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’
If then God gave to them the same gift as he did also to us, when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”
When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”

whatGodIsSaying.headline: God plays no favorites; the barrier of ancient hostility is torn down, and the Holy Spirit is poured out on every hungry heart that believes.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: For over a thousand years, the wall between Jew and Gentile had been virtually impenetrable. Strict kosher dietary laws and rabbinic traditions forbade a faithful Jew from even entering the home of an uncircumcised Gentile, let alone eating at their table. But God prepared both sides of the divine collision: while Cornelius was praying in Caesarea, Peter was up on a rooftop in Joppa having a vision of clean and unclean animals lowered in a sheet. God's thunderous decree shattered Peter's prejudice: 'What God has cleansed, you must not call unclean!' When Peter arrived in Cornelius' living room, he found an Italian Roman officer who had packed his entire family, friends, and soldiers into the room, saying: 'We are all here present in the sight of God to hear all things commanded you by the Lord!' What a preacher's dream! Peter opened his mouth and confessed his own repentance: 'Truly I perceive that God does not show favoritism!' And as Peter proclaimed the forgiveness of sins through Jesus' name, the Holy Spirit couldn't even wait for the altar call—He interrupted the sermon! The Holy Spirit fell upon Roman Gentiles with rushing power, just like at Pentecost. The circumcision party from Jerusalem stood with mouths wide open. God had granted repentance unto eternal life to the Gentiles! In Christ, there is no racial elite; the ground at the foot of the cross is completely level.

lessons.lesson: God does not show partiality based on race, nationality, or social background.
lessons.detail: Every human being who fears God and trusts in Jesus Christ is fully accepted into His family; any form of racial or ethnic prejudice violates the Gospel.
lessons.question: Do you harbor any subtle prejudice or superiority toward people of different cultural or national backgrounds?

lessons.lesson: Disciplined prayer and generous giving are remembered in the courts of heaven.
lessons.detail: Even before he knew the full Gospel, Cornelius' sincere prayers and alms ascended as a sweet-smelling memorial before God, who sent him the Light.
lessons.question: Is your prayer life and financial generosity creating an enduring memorial before God?

lessons.lesson: God will dismantle our religious traditions to reach people who are hungry for truth.
lessons.detail: Peter had to unlearn lifelong kosher taboos so he could step into a Gentile home; we must discard cultural barriers that hinder Gospel outreach.
lessons.question: What personal comfort zones or cultural traditions are you unwilling to sacrifice to reach outsiders for Christ?

lessons.lesson: The Holy Spirit falls directly upon hearts that listen eagerly to the preaching of Jesus.
lessons.detail: While Peter was still speaking of forgiveness through Jesus' name, the Holy Spirit fell upon the listeners; hungry faith receives instant divine power.
lessons.question: Do you approach the preaching of God's Word with an expectant, hungry heart ready to be filled by the Spirit?

quiz.question: What military title and regiment did Cornelius hold in Caesarea?
quiz.explanation: Acts 10:1 notes that Cornelius was 'a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment.'

quiz.question: What did the angel tell Cornelius about his prayers and gifts to the needy in Acts 10:4?
options: They were insufficient to please God
They have gone up for a memorial before God
They must be repeated in Latin
They should be paid to the temple
quiz.explanation: The angel said: 'Your prayers and your gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before God.'

quiz.question: What monumental declaration did Peter make in Acts 10:34?
options: Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism
quiz.explanation: Peter declared: 'Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism (is no respecter of persons).'

quiz.question: The Jewish believers who accompanied Peter were furious and refused to let the Gentiles be baptized with water.
quiz.explanation: False. They were amazed that the Holy Spirit fell on them, and Peter commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

quiz.question: What was the final verdict of the Jerusalem church in Acts 11:18 after Peter explained what happened?
options: Peter must pay a fine to the Sanhedrin
Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!
Gentiles may only sit in the back rows
quiz.explanation: They held their peace and glorified God, saying: 'Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Heavenly Father, Lord of all nations, I praise You that You do not show favoritism! You broke down the dividing wall of hostility through the cross of Jesus Christ, pouring out Your Holy Spirit upon Gentiles and Jews alike. Forgive me for any lingering prejudice, partiality, or cultural pride that would treat another human being as less than precious in Your sight. Make my home a sanctuary like Cornelius'—a place where family and friends gather with eager hearts to hear the Word of the Lord. Fall afresh upon us today, Holy Spirit, and let Your saving grace reach to the ends of the earth.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism; but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Praise God that His covenant of grace has welcomed you in, and pray for unreached people groups around the world today.

304.season: Syrian Antioch: Seeing the Grace of God and Gathering the Disciples
304.theme: Generous spiritual leaders rejoice in fresh revivals and bring in others to disciple the harvest.

memoryVerse.text: who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad. He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would remain near to the Lord.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Insecure leaders criticize or stifle movements they cannot control, but godly leaders like Barnabas rejoice when they see God's grace at work, encouraging believers and enlisting others to mentor the harvest.

cramData.firstLetters: w, w h h c, a h s t g o G, w g. H e t a, t w p o h t w r n t t L.

profile.title: Barnabas at Syrian Antioch: The Discerning Shepherd Who Launched the Gentile Super-Church
profile.who: Barnabas of Cyprus, dispatched from Jerusalem to investigate reports of an unprompted, spontaneous revival among Greek Gentiles in Syrian Antioch; instead of squashing the revival under legalistic rules, he saw the undeniable grace of God, rejoiced, traveled to Tarsus to track down Saul, and brought him back to Antioch where disciples were first called 'Christians.'
profile.whenAndWhere: Antioch of Syria (the third largest city in the Roman Empire), circa AD 41–43.
profile.family: Levite from Cyprus; cousin of John Mark.
keyMoments: Arriving in cosmopolitan Antioch after anonymous believers from Cyprus and Cyrene preached Jesus to the Greeks.
Looking past cultural chaos to see the genuine grace of God, exploding with joy rather than suspicion.
Exhorting the new converts to remain faithful to the Lord with unwavering purpose of heart.
Realizing the magnitude of the harvest and traveling to Tarsus to search for Saul, bringing him back to co-lead the church.
Teaching together with Saul for a whole year, seeing such profound transformation that disciples were first called 'Christians' at Antioch.
profile.strengths: Freedom from jealousy and insecurity, supernatural ability to see God's grace in unexpected places, partnership and team leadership.
profile.failures: None in this season; described by Luke as 'a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith.'

scripture.title: The Church in Antioch and Barnabas Seeks Saul

verses.text: They therefore who were scattered abroad by the oppression that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except only to Jews.
But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus.
The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
The report concerning them came to the ears of the assembly which was in Jerusalem. They sent out Barnabas to go as far as Antioch,
who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad. He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would remain near to the Lord.
For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and many people were added to the Lord.
Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul.
When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

scripture.title: Famine Relief and the Multiplication of the Word

verses.text: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he didn’t give God the glory, and he was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of God grew and multiplied.
Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their service, also taking with them John whose surname was Mark.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: A truly great spiritual leader does not seek personal empire; they rejoice in God's grace and recruit others to share the platform.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Antioch was the third greatest metropolis in the Roman world, notorious for luxury, moral decadence, and chariot racing. Yet into this pagan cauldron, ordinary, unnamed believers from Cyprus and Cyrene began talking about Jesus to Greek pagans. The hand of the Lord fell, and a massive revival erupted! When rumors reached the mother church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to investigate. A small-minded bureaucrat would have inspected the converts for liturgical errors, imposed heavy rituals, or tried to monopolize control. But look at Barnabas: 'When he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad!' He had spiritual eyes that looked right through cultural differences to recognize God's fingerprint. Luke gives him a glowing tribute: 'For he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith.' But Barnabas did something even more remarkable: seeing that this new Gentile church needed rigorous theological grounding, he didn't try to build a solo kingdom. He got on a boat, traveled to Tarsus, hunted down Saul, pulled him out of obscurity, and shared the pulpit with him! For an entire year, they poured their lives into discipling converts until the pagan city noticed that these people acted so much like the Messiah that they coined a new word: *Christianoi*—'Christians' ('little Christs').

lessons.lesson: Learn to recognize and celebrate the grace of God even when it appears in unexpected packaging.
lessons.detail: Barnabas was glad when he saw God's grace at work among pagan Greeks; we must never allow religious traditionalism to blind us to fresh moves of the Spirit.
lessons.question: Are you quick to rejoice when God uses other churches or ministries that look different from your own?

lessons.lesson: Spiritual greatness involves sharing the spotlight and bringing others into their God-given destiny.
lessons.detail: Barnabas could have kept Antioch as his personal pulpit, but he traveled to Tarsus to bring Saul onto the team; humility elevates others.
lessons.question: Are you actively looking for opportunities to mentor, promote, and share leadership with others?

lessons.lesson: Deep, consistent discipleship transforms a church into a reflection of Jesus Christ.
lessons.detail: A full year of systematic teaching in the Word produced believers whose character was so undeniably Christlike that outsiders named them 'Christians.'
lessons.question: Does your daily conduct at work and at home make the name 'Christian' honorable in the eyes of onlookers?

lessons.lesson: Generous churches look beyond their own borders to relieve the suffering of other saints.
lessons.detail: When famine hit Judea, the young church in Antioch immediately collected relief funds and sent Barnabas and Saul to deliver it to Jerusalem.
lessons.question: How is your local church family actively supporting poor and persecuted believers in other parts of the world?

quiz.question: Who were the bold, unnamed believers who first began preaching the Lord Jesus to Hellenists (Greeks) in Antioch?
quiz.explanation: Acts 11:20 says: 'there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who... spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus.'

quiz.question: What was Barnabas' reaction when he arrived in Antioch in Acts 11:23?
options: He demanded they return to Jerusalem
When he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad
quiz.explanation: Acts 11:23 notes: 'who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad.'

quiz.question: Where did Barnabas travel to find Saul and bring him back to Antioch?
quiz.explanation: Acts 11:25 states: 'Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul.'

quiz.question: The disciples were first called 'Christians' in the city of Jerusalem.
quiz.explanation: False. Acts 11:26 explicitly reveals: 'The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.'

quiz.question: How does Luke describe Barnabas' personal spiritual character in Acts 11:24?
options: A strict disciplinarian of the law
A good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith
quiz.explanation: Luke writes: 'For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith...'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Head of the Church, make me a good servant like Barnabas—full of the Holy Spirit, full of faith, and free from all petty jealousy. Give me eyes to recognize Your sovereign grace wherever it is working, even in unexpected places and people. Deliver me from the insecurity that tries to build personal kingdoms or hold onto platforms. Teach me to encourage young believers with purpose of heart to remain near to You. Raise up apostolic teams in our generation who will pour themselves out in discipleship until the whole world sees Christ in us.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad. He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would remain near to the Lord.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Evaluate your heart: celebrate the success of someone else's ministry or work without a single drop of envy.

305.season: Herod's Prison & Mary's House: The Sleeping Apostle, the Angel, and the Maid
305.theme: Persistent corporate prayer unleashes angelic deliverance, shattering iron gates while believers are amazed.

memoryVerse.text: Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: When political tyranny locks the doors and chains God's servants between guards, the fervent, unceasing intercession of the church holds the keys that can summon angels and fling open iron gates.

cramData.firstLetters: P t w k i t p, b c p w m b t a t G f h.

profile.title: Peter, the Angel, and Rhoda the Servant Girl: The Prison Break of Faith
profile.who: Simon Peter, arrested by King Herod Agrippa I during Passover and scheduled for public execution the next morning, sleeping peacefully bound between two Roman soldiers; while the church engaged in round-the-clock unceasing intercession at Mary's house, an angel shattered the chains, led Peter through iron gates, and left him knocking on the outer door where a servant maid named Rhoda was so overjoyed she forgot to open it.
profile.whenAndWhere: The Fortress Antonia prison and the house of Mary (mother of John Mark), Jerusalem, Passover, circa AD 44.
profile.family: Rhoda: a young servant maid in the house of Mary, mother of John Mark.
keyMoments: Herod Agrippa executing James the brother of John and arresting Peter to please the mob.
Peter sleeping soundly on the eve of his execution, bound with two heavy iron chains between two soldiers with sixteen guards on duty.
An angel of the Lord appearing in a flash of light, striking Peter on the side to wake him, and causing the chains to fall off silently.
Walking past two guard posts and watching the city's massive iron gate swing open automatically (*automate*).

Peter knocking at the gate of Mary's house where prayer was raging; Rhoda recognizing his voice, running back inside screaming with joy without unlocking the door, while the praying church argued: 'You are crazy!'
profile.strengths: Peter: astonishing peace resting in God's promises. Rhoda: joyful faith and instant recognition of Peter's voice. Church: persistent intercession.
profile.failures: The praying church struggled with unbelief, assuming Rhoda had seen Peter's ghost rather than believing their prayers were answered.

scripture.title: Peter's Miraculous Deliverance from Herod's Prison

verses.text: Now about that time, King Herod stretched out his hands to oppress some of the assembly.
He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
When he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This was during the days of unleavened bread.
Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.
The same night when Herod was about to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Guards in front of the door kept the prison.
Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side, and woke him up, saying, “Shake off your chains!” His chains fell off from his hands.

When they were past the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them by itself. They went out, and passed on through one street; and immediately the angel departed from him.
Thinking about that, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John whose surname was Mark, where many were gathered together and were praying.
When Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a girl named Rhoda came to answer.
When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy, but ran in, and told that Peter stood before the gate.
They said to her, “You are crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”
But Peter continued knocking. When they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.

scripture.title: The Angel of Yahweh Encamped Around Those Who Fear Him

verses.text: I sought Yahweh, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
The angel of Yahweh encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.
Oh taste and see that Yahweh is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: When earth locks its heaviest chains around you, heaven responds to persistent prayer by sending angels to open iron gates.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Look at the high-stakes drama of Acts 12. Herod Agrippa had just executed the Apostle James with the sword, and seeing the political boost it gave his poll numbers, threw Peter on death row under maximum security: four squads of four Roman soldiers each (16 guards!). Tomorrow morning, Peter was scheduled to be led out to the chopping block. How was Peter spending his final night on earth? He was fast asleep! Bound between two armed Roman soldiers with heavy iron manacles, Peter was snoring so deeply that the angel had to hit him in the ribs to wake him up! Why could Peter sleep? Because back in John 21:18, Jesus had prophesied that Peter would die when he was an old man with gray hair; Peter knew he wasn't old yet, so Herod couldn't kill him tomorrow! He rested in God's promises. Meanwhile, across town in Mary's home, the church was engaged in *ektenes* prayer—the same word used of Jesus praying in agony in Gethsemane: stretched-out, unceasing corporate intercession. The angel dropped the chains, walked Peter past two armed checkpoints, and the massive city iron gate swung open automatically (*automate*). When Peter knocked at the gate, Rhoda recognized his voice and lost her mind with joy, leaving Peter standing in the dark street knocking! Even when the praying church struggled with doubt ('You're crazy! It's his ghost!'), God answered their prayers anyway. God's mercy is greater than our imperfect faith.

lessons.lesson: Deep trust in God's promises produces peaceful rest even in the shadow of crisis.
lessons.detail: Peter slept soundly on death row because his soul was anchored in Christ's prophetic word; anxiety flees where God's promises are trusted.
lessons.question: Can you sleep peacefully tonight, knowing that your life and future are held in God's sovereign hands?

lessons.lesson: Persistent, united corporate prayer possesses power to shatter impossible spiritual chains.
lessons.detail: The church didn't mount a political protest or storm the fortress; they gathered to pray unceasingly, and God dispatched an angel from glory.
lessons.question: How committed are you to gathering with other believers for fervent, united intercession?

lessons.lesson: God frequently answers our prayers even while our fragile faith is still struggling with doubt.
lessons.detail: The believers were praying for Peter's release, yet when he stood at the gate, they told Rhoda she was crazy; God is gracious to answer weak faith.
lessons.question: Are you surprised when God actually answers your prayers, or praying with expectant confidence?

lessons.lesson: No prison walls, Roman chains, or iron gates can prevent God from delivering His servants.
lessons.detail: The angel of Yahweh walked through locked doors and opened iron gates without a crowbar; God makes a way where there is no human way.
lessons.question: What 'iron gate' or locked obstacle in your life do you need to entrust to God's supernatural power today?

quiz.question: Which apostle had King Herod Agrippa executed with the sword right before arresting Peter?
quiz.explanation: Acts 12:2 states: 'He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.'

quiz.question: What was Peter doing the night before Herod intended to bring him out for public execution?
options: Sleeping soundly between two soldiers, bound with two chains
Singing hymns at the top of his voice
quiz.explanation: Acts 12:6 notes: 'The same night... Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains.'

quiz.question: What did the massive iron gate leading into the city do when Peter and the angel approached it?
options: The soldiers unlocked it with a key
It opened to them by itself (automatically)
Peter broke it down with a hammer
quiz.explanation: Acts 12:10 says: 'the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them by itself.'

quiz.question: When Rhoda told the praying believers that Peter was standing outside the gate, they immediately believed her with great joy.
quiz.explanation: False. They argued: 'You are crazy!' and assumed it must be his angel.

quiz.question: According to Psalm 34:7, who encamps around those who fear Yahweh and delivers them?
quiz.explanation: Psalm 34:7 proclaims: 'The angel of Yahweh encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Almighty God, You are the Lord who shatters chains and swings open iron gates! Thank You that You encamp around those who fear You and deliver them out of all their troubles. Forgive my anxious, sleepless nights when trials surround me; grant me Peter's supernatural peace to sleep in confidence upon Your unbreakable promises. Awaken in my church a spirit of constant, unceasing corporate prayer. When impossible obstacles stand before me like iron gates, stretch out Your hand and make a way where there is no human way. Surprise my feeble faith with Your overwhelming answers, and let Your name be glorified.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Bring your most difficult 'locked door' before God right now: ask Him to shatter the chains and open the gate.

306.season: The Sending from Antioch: Set Apart by the Holy Spirit for Global Mission
306.theme: Worship and fasting form the spiritual womb from which the Holy Spirit launches global mission.

memoryVerse.text: As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Global mission does not originate in human strategic planning committees, but in the presence of God as believers worship, fast, and listen to the voice of the Holy Spirit.

cramData.firstLetters: A t s t L a f, t H S s, “S B a S f m, f t w t w I h c t.”

profile.title: Paul and Barnabas Commissioned at Antioch: The Launch of the First Missionary Journey
profile.who: Barnabas and Saul, serving as part of a diverse multicultural team of prophets and teachers in the Syrian Antioch church (including Simeon Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, childhood companion of Herod the tetrarch); while worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit spoke clearly, commissioning Barnabas and Saul for the historic First Missionary Journey into Cyprus and Galatia.
profile.whenAndWhere: The church at Syrian Antioch, circa AD 46–47.
profile.family: Apostolic missionary partners; accompanied by John Mark as their assistant.
keyMoments: Leading a multi-ethnic, racially diverse leadership team in worship, prayer, and fasting.
Hearing the distinct, audible or prophetic voice of the Holy Spirit: 'Separate Barnabas and Saul for me...'
The church fasting and praying again, laying hands on them, and releasing them to sail from Seleucia to Cyprus.
Confronting Elymas the sorcerer before Sergius Paulus the Roman proconsul on Cyprus, where Saul is first called Paul.
Proclaiming Jesus boldly in the synagogue of Pisidian Antioch, declaring justification by faith that the Law of Moses could never grant.
profile.strengths: Deep devotion to worship and fasting, sensitivity to the Holy Spirit's guidance, fearless apostolic courage across pagan territories.
profile.failures: Later experienced a sharp disagreement over whether to take John Mark on the second journey after Mark deserted them in Pamphylia (Acts 15:37-39).

scripture.title: The Holy Spirit Sends Barnabas and Saul from Antioch

verses.text: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.
But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him,
“Be it known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins;
and by him everyone who believes is justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.”
As the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of God. As many as were appointed to eternal life believed.

scripture.title: A Light to the Nations to the Ends of the Earth

verses.text: Listen, islands, to me. Listen, you peoples from afar: Yahweh has called me from the womb; from the inside of my mother he has mentioned my name.

Now Yahweh, who formed me from the womb to be his servant, says to bring Jacob again to him, and that Israel be gathered to him; for I am honorable in the eyes of Yahweh, and my God has become my strength.

Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”

whatGodIsSaying.headline: When a church prioritizes unhurried worship and fasting, the Holy Spirit speaks with clarity and launches world-changing movements.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: Look at the extraordinary leadership team assembled in Syrian Antioch in Acts 13:1: Barnabas (a wealthy Levite from Cyprus), Simeon called Niger ('the black man,' likely an African), Lucius of Cyrene (from North Africa), Manaen (a member of the royal aristocracy raised alongside Herod the tetrarch), and Saul (the former Pharisee and brilliant scholar). What an astonishing portrait of Gospel unity! Wealthy and poor, African and Jew, royal and commoner, kneeling together in one accord! And what were they doing? Luke uses the word *leitourgounton*—they were ministering to the Lord and fasting. They weren't just brainstorming human marketing strategies; they were loving Jesus! And out of that holy atmosphere of worship and fasting, the Holy Spirit spoke: 'Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.' Notice what the church did next: Barnabas and Saul were their two premier preachers and best leaders. Human possessiveness would have protested: 'We can't let our two best leaders leave Antioch!' But a Spirit-filled church holds its best with open hands. They fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them out. That sailing ship leaving Seleucia changed the history of Western civilization and the eternal destiny of billions of souls. Give God your best, and watch Him shake the nations.

lessons.lesson: The Holy Spirit reveals His strategic plans to believers who minister to the Lord in worship and fasting.
lessons.detail: Spiritual guidance flows out of intimate worship; when we quiet our appetites and focus on Christ, the voice of the Spirit becomes crystal clear.
lessons.question: How often do you incorporate unhurried worship and fasting into your spiritual rhythm to seek God's direction?

lessons.lesson: A healthy church must be willing to send out its best resources for global kingdom harvest.
lessons.detail: Antioch willingly released their two greatest teachers to take the Gospel to unreached pagan regions; selfish hoarding stifles spiritual growth.
lessons.question: Is your local church focused primarily on internal comfort, or actively sending and supporting global mission?

lessons.lesson: True Gospel justification delivers freedom that the Law of Moses could never provide.
lessons.detail: Paul boldly preached that through faith in Jesus, every believer is completely justified from all guilt that moral laws could never erase.
lessons.question: Are you resting in the complete justification provided by Christ's blood, or still striving to justify yourself?

lessons.lesson: God's redemptive purpose has always been to make His salvation a light to every nation on earth.
lessons.detail: God told the Messiah that reaching one nation was 'too small a thing'—He appointed Christ to be a blazing light to the ends of the earth.
lessons.question: Does your personal vision for God's Kingdom align with His passion to reach every tribe, tongue, and nation?

quiz.question: What spiritual activities was the leadership team in Antioch engaged in when the Holy Spirit spoke in Acts 13:2?
options: Drafting a new budget and political lobbying
quiz.explanation: Acts 13:2 states: 'As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said...'

quiz.question: What specific command did the Holy Spirit give to the church at Antioch?
options: Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them
quiz.explanation: The Spirit commanded: 'Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.'

quiz.question: To what Mediterranean island did Barnabas and Saul sail first on their missionary journey?
quiz.explanation: Acts 13:4 records: 'they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.'

quiz.question: In Acts 13:39, Paul taught that keeping the Law of Moses is the only way to be fully justified before God.
quiz.explanation: False. Paul declared that through Jesus everyone who believes is justified from all things from which you could NOT be justified by the Law of Moses.

quiz.question: According to Isaiah 49:6, what did God appoint His Servant to be to the ends of the earth?
options: A judge with an iron rod
A light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth
A silent prophet in the desert
quiz.explanation: God proclaims: 'I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God Almighty, You are the Lord of the harvest who calls, separates, and sends Your servants to the nations! Forgive me for becoming absorbed in my own small plans and human strategies. Teach me the sacred posture of Antioch: to minister unhurried worship to You, to fast, to listen, and to yield to the voice of the Holy Spirit. Give my church a global missionary heartbeat. Break every spirit of possessiveness, and help us joyfully release our best prayers, finances, and people so that the light of Jesus Christ may shine into the darkest corners of the earth.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Set aside a season of quiet worship and fasting this week: ask the Holy Spirit what work He is calling you to do.

307.season: Lystra and Derbe: Stoned, Raised, and Strengthening the Churches
307.theme: Persevering through hardships and stoning confirms that God's kingdom is worth every tribulation.

memoryVerse.text: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: The Christian life is not an immune bubble of prosperity; trials, persecution, and afflictions are the normal, paved road through which God matures our souls and ushers us into the fullness of His Kingdom.

cramData.firstLetters: c t s o t d, e t t c i t f, a t t m a w m e i G’ K.

profile.title: Paul and Barnabas at Lystra: From Deified Gods to Stoned Preachers
profile.who: Paul and Barnabas, preaching throughout Galatia on their first missionary journey; after healing a congenital cripple in pagan Lystra, the fickle crowd attempted to worship them as Greek gods (Zeus and Hermes), but when hostile agitators arrived from Antioch and Iconium, the mob stoned Paul, dragged his battered body outside the city, leaving him for dead—only for Paul to stand back up, re-enter the city, and return to strengthen the young churches.
profile.whenAndWhere: Lystra and Derbe in southern Galatia (modern Turkey), circa AD 47–48.
profile.family: Missionary partners; met young Timothy and his family in Lystra (Acts 16:1).
keyMoments: Healing a man lame from birth in Lystra who had never walked, commanding him: 'Stand upright on your feet!'
The pagan crowds shouting in Lycaonian: 'The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!' calling Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes.
Tearing their clothes and running into the mob to stop sacrifices: 'We are men of like passions with you, and preach good news to you, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God!'
Jews from Antioch and Iconium persuading the crowds, stoning Paul with heavy rocks, and dragging his unconscious body outside the walls for dead.

As disciples stood weeping around him, Paul miraculously stood up, walked right back into Lystra, and traveled back through every hostile city strengthening disciples: 'Through many tribulations we must enter the Kingdom of God!'
profile.strengths: Unshakable tenacity, refusal to accept idolatrous human worship, resilient physical and spiritual courage.
profile.failures: None recorded in this heroic missionary campaign; glorious perseverance under brutal suffering.

scripture.title: The Stoning at Lystra and Strengthening the Disciples

verses.text: At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.
He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,
said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” He leaped up and walked.
When the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”
But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they tore their clothes, and sprang into the multitude, crying out,

“Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;
But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
When they had preached the Good News to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.

scripture.title: Persevering in the Face of Persecution

verses.text: But you followed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, steadfastness,
persecutions, and sufferings: what things happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra; what persecutions I endured. Out of them all the Lord delivered me.
Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.
But you remain in the things which you have learned and have been assured of, knowing from whom you have learned them.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Popular applause and worldly hostility are both fickle illusions; true kingdom impact is forged through steadfast endurance in trials.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: The dramatic story of Lystra exposes the utter fickleness of human opinion. One day, the pagan crowds were so dazzled by the healing of the lame man that they brought oxen and floral wreaths to sacrifice to Paul and Barnabas as Greek gods! Paul and Barnabas tore their tunics in horror, refusing to steal God's glory. But look at what happened just hours later: agitators arrived from Iconium, poisoned the minds of the crowd, and that very same mob picked up jagged stones and hurled them at Paul's head until he lay battered, bloody, and limp in the dust! They dragged his bruised body outside the city gate and dumped it in the garbage, assuming he was dead. Human applause is cheap: one moment they shout 'Gods!' and the next moment they shout 'Stone him!' But look at Paul's supernatural resilience: as the devastated young disciples (including teenage Timothy) stood weeping around his bruised body, Paul blinked his bloody eyes, sat up, got back onto his feet, and walked right back into the city that had just stoned him! And instead of retreating home to nurse his wounds, he re-traced his steps back through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch, strengthening the young converts with this immortal truth: 'Through many tribulations we must enter into the Kingdom of God!' Difficulties are not a sign that you are on the wrong road; they are proof that you are following in the footsteps of the Cross-Bearing King.

lessons.lesson: Never feed on the fickle applause of human praise; give all glory to the living God.
lessons.detail: Paul and Barnabas tore their clothes rather than accept idolatrous flattery; those who live for human approval will crumble when human disapproval arrives.
lessons.question: Are you addicted to the praise and compliments of people, or anchored solely in God's approval?

lessons.lesson: Expect tribulation as the normal path of authentic Christian discipleship.
lessons.detail: Paul did not promise new converts an easy, problem-free existence; he warned them clearly: 'All who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.'
lessons.question: Do you view hardships as evidence of God's absence, or as the refining fires that mature your faith?

lessons.lesson: Resilience in Christ empowers you to rise back up after crushing blows.
lessons.detail: Stoned and left for dead, Paul rose back up by God's supernatural power; the righteous may fall seven times, but the Lord raises them up.
lessons.question: Has a recent discouragement or painful blow knocked you down? Will you ask the Lord for the strength to stand back up today?

lessons.lesson: Shepherding young believers requires strengthening their souls to persevere in faith.
lessons.detail: Evangelism is only half the commission; Paul risked his life to return to hostile cities to confirm and establish disciples in enduring faith.
lessons.question: How are you practically helping newer or younger believers stay grounded in their walk with Christ?

quiz.question: What Greek gods did the pagan crowds in Lystra mistakenly assume Barnabas and Paul were?
quiz.explanation: Acts 14:12 says: 'They called Barnabas, “Zeus”, and Paul, “Hermes”, because he was the chief speaker.'

quiz.question: How did Paul and Barnabas respond when the priest of Zeus brought oxen and garlands to sacrifice to them?
options: They tore their clothes and sprang into the multitude, crying out to turn to the living God
quiz.explanation: They tore their clothes and rushed in, shouting that they were merely mortal men preaching the living God who made heaven and earth.

quiz.question: What violent act did the hostile mob inflict on Paul at Lystra, leaving him for dead?
options: They stoned him and dragged him out of the city
They threw him into a pit of lions
They locked him in chains in a cellar
quiz.explanation: Acts 14:19 states: 'they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.'

quiz.question: When the disciples stood around Paul's battered body, he rose up and walked back into the city.
quiz.explanation: True. Acts 14:20 records: 'as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city.'

quiz.question: What essential message did Paul and Barnabas preach to confirm the disciples in Acts 14:22?
options: You will quickly become wealthy merchants
Through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom
Roman law will protect your investments
All suffering will vanish next year
quiz.explanation: They exhorted disciples 'that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of unconquerable strength, You are the living God who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them! Deliver me from the snare of living for human praise or shrinking back from worldly reproach. When stones of affliction, misunderstanding, or persecution strike my life, grant me the supernatural resilience of Paul. Give me grace to stand back up, to brush off the dust, and to continue preaching the Good News with undaunted courage. Confirm my soul in the faith, Lord, and remind me that through many tribulations we enter into Your glorious Kingdom. Out of all trials, You will deliver me!
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Offer up your current affliction or hardship to the Lord: thank Him that it is preparing you for eternal kingdom glory.

308.season: The Jerusalem Council: Guarding the Purity of Grace
308.theme: Wise council leadership guards the purity of the gospel: salvation by grace through faith alone.

memoryVerse.text: “But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.”
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: Salvation is identical for all people across all eras and cultures: completely unearned, through the unconditional grace of Jesus Christ alone, without legalistic human additions.

cramData.firstLetters: “B w b t w a s t t g o t L J, j a t a.”

profile.title: James the Just: The Wisdom of the Jerusalem Council
profile.who: The biological half-brother of Jesus who did not believe during Christ's earthly ministry, but became a pillar of the early church after an appearance by the Risen Lord (1 Corinthians 15:7); presiding over the historic Jerusalem Council in Acts 15, he harmonized Peter's testimony and Paul's mission with Amos' prophecy to establish that Gentile converts are saved by grace alone without circumcision.
profile.whenAndWhere: The Council in Jerusalem, circa AD 49–50.
profile.family: Son of Mary and Joseph, half-brother of Jesus and Jude; elder of the Jerusalem church.
keyMoments: Initially skeptical of Jesus' messianic claims during His earthly ministry (John 7:5).
Experiencing a personal encounter with the resurrected Christ that shattered his doubt.
Rising to lead the Jerusalem assembly as its premier elder and respected moderator.
Listening attentively as Peter, Paul, and Barnabas testified of Gentile conversions.
Rendering the decisive verdict: 'Therefore my judgment is that we don’t trouble those from among the Gentiles who turn to God,' preserving Gospel grace forever.
profile.strengths: Deep wisdom, biblical grounding in the prophets, unshakeable peacemaking ability, personal holiness and integrity.
profile.failures: Early skepticism and unbelief regarding his brother Jesus prior to the Resurrection.

scripture.title: The Council of Jerusalem and the Triumph of Grace

verses.text: When there had been much discussion, Peter rose up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that a good while ago God made a choice among you, that by my mouth the nations should hear the word of the Good News, and believe.
God, who knows the heart, testified to them, giving them the Holy Spirit, just like he did to us.
He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
Now therefore why do you tempt God, that you should put a yoke on the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.”
After they were silent, James answered, “Brothers, listen to me.
Simeon has reported how God first visited the nations, to take out of them a people for his name.
Therefore my judgment is that we don’t trouble those from among the Gentiles who turn to God,”

scripture.title: Preserving the Truth of the Gospel without Compromise

verses.text: This was because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who stole in to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage;
to whom we gave no place in the way of subjection, not for an hour, that the truth of the Good News might continue with you.

and when they perceived the grace that was given to me, James and Cephas and John, they who were reputed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision.

yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ, and not by the works of the law, because no flesh will be justified by the works of the law.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: Salvation is a gift of pure grace through faith alone; no human ritual or moral striving can be added to the finished work of Christ.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: The Council of Jerusalem was the most critical doctrinal crisis in church history. Some believers from the party of the Pharisees insisted: 'Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved!' If that view had prevailed, Christianity would have degenerated into an exclusive, legalistic Jewish sect. But Peter stood up and made the radical declaration of Acts 15:11: 'We believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are!' Notice Peter's phrasing: he didn't say the Gentiles are saved like the Jews; he said the Jews are saved like the Gentiles—by pure, unmerited grace! Then James, the revered leader known as 'James the Just' for his strict personal observance of the Torah, stepped forward. He didn't appeal to emotional rhetoric; he quoted the Prophet Amos. He proved that God had always planned to rebuild David's fallen tent so that all nations could seek the Lord. James rendered his holy verdict: 'We must not trouble those Gentiles who are turning to God!' True spiritual leadership guards the liberty of the Gospel. You are not saved by Jesus PLUS your performance, your rituals, or your religious heritage. You are saved by Jesus alone.

lessons.lesson: Never add human conditions or legalistic rules to the pure Gospel of grace.
lessons.detail: Adding religious rituals or human works as prerequisites for salvation distorts the Gospel and places an unbearable yoke on believers' necks.
lessons.question: Are you tempted to believe that God's love for you depends on how well you maintain spiritual disciplines?

lessons.lesson: Wise conflict resolution listens to all sides and anchors decisions in the Word of God.
lessons.detail: James listened patiently to Peter, Paul, and Barnabas, and then anchored his final judgment in the prophetic Scriptures of Amos.
lessons.question: When conflicts arise in your church or family, do you seek emotional compromise or biblical clarity?

lessons.lesson: God makes zero distinction in His saving mercy between diverse racial and cultural groups.
lessons.detail: God cleanses hearts by faith alone, pouring out the same Holy Spirit on people of every nation and background without favoritism.
lessons.question: Does your local church welcome people of diverse backgrounds with open, grace-filled arms?

lessons.lesson: Christian liberty should be exercised with loving sensitivity toward others' consciences.
lessons.detail: While liberating Gentiles from circumcision, James asked them to avoid practices deeply offensive to Jewish neighbors to preserve fellowship.
lessons.question: Are you willing to limit your personal liberties in love so that you do not cause a brother or sister to stumble?

quiz.question: What controversy brought Paul and Barnabas to the Council of Jerusalem in Acts 15?
options: Men teaching that Gentiles must be circumcised according to Moses to be saved
A debate over which translation of Scripture to use
Arguments about building a new cathedral
quiz.explanation: Certain men from Judea taught: 'Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you can’t be saved.'

quiz.question: What memorable declaration did Peter make in Acts 15:11 regarding salvation?
options: We are saved by keeping the Sabbath and dietary laws
We believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are
Only the circumcised will enter the Kingdom
Works are the sole basis of justification
quiz.explanation: Peter affirmed: 'we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.'

quiz.question: Which elder gave the decisive summary and judgment at the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15:13-19?
quiz.explanation: James answered: 'Therefore my judgment is that we don’t trouble those from among the Gentiles who turn to God...'

quiz.question: According to Galatians 2:16, flesh can easily be justified before God by doing the works of the law.
quiz.explanation: False. Paul insists: 'because no flesh will be justified by the works of the law.'

quiz.question: Which three leaders in Jerusalem were recognized as 'pillars' of the church in Galatians 2:9?
quiz.explanation: Paul mentions: 'James and Cephas and John, they who were reputed to be pillars...'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of all grace, I praise You that salvation is not an unbearable yoke of human legalism, but a free gift of pure mercy through the blood of Jesus Christ! Thank You that You cleanse my heart by faith alone. Forgive me for any legalistic tendencies to judge other believers or to measure my worth before You by my religious performance. Give wisdom and discernment to leaders in Your church today. Help us guard the purity of the Gospel, tear down every unnecessary obstacle in the way of searching souls, and walk in loving unity across every cultural divide.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Rest your conscience completely in Christ's finished work: declare aloud that you are saved by grace alone.

309.season: The Sharp Contention at Antioch: Second Chances and Restored Champions
309.theme: Patient, restorative mentoring breathes new life into quitters, turning them into faithful servants of Christ.

memoryVerse.text: Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: God is the God of the second chance; although John Mark deserted Paul and Barnabas in Pamphylia, Barnabas' patient, loving investment restored Mark into the author of the second Gospel and a worker Paul desperately valued in his final hours.

cramData.firstLetters: O L i w m. T M, a b h w y, f h i u t m f s.

profile.title: Barnabas and John Mark: The Mentor Who Refused to Write Off a Quitter
profile.who: Barnabas and his young cousin John Mark; after Mark deserted the missionary team at Perga during the first journey (Acts 13:13), Paul flatly refused to take him on the second journey, causing a sharp contention that split Paul and Barnabas; Barnabas took Mark under his wing to Cyprus, patiently restoring him into an indispensable minister who eventually wrote the Gospel of Mark.
profile.whenAndWhere: Antioch of Syria and the island of Cyprus, circa AD 50.
profile.family: John Mark: son of Mary of Jerusalem, cousin of Barnabas (Colossians 4:10).
keyMoments: John Mark abandoning Paul and Barnabas in Pamphylia and returning home to his mother in Jerusalem.
Paul proposing a second journey to revisit the churches, while Barnabas insisted on taking Mark.
A sharp disagreement (*paroxysmos*) erupting between Paul and Barnabas, causing them to part company.
Barnabas refusing to discard his struggling cousin, sailing with Mark to Cyprus for patient, long-term mentoring.
Years later, Paul writing from Roman death row to Timothy: 'Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service!'
profile.strengths: Barnabas: unwavering commitment to restore fallen workers, patience, fatherly grace. Mark: humility to accept correction and persevere.
profile.failures: Mark: deserted the mission field out of fear, homesickness, or immaturity on the first journey.

scripture.title: The Sharp Disagreement Over John Mark

verses.text: After some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let’s return now and visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
Barnabas planned to take John, who was called Mark, with them also.
But Paul didn’t think that it was good to take with them someone who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia, and hadn’t gone with them to the work.
Then a sharp contention arose, so that they separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark with him, and sailed away to Cyprus,
but Paul chose Silas, and went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.

scripture.title: Paul's Final Commendation of Mark

verses.text: Give diligence to come to me soon,
for Demas left me, having loved this present world, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
But I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
Bring the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, when you come, and the books, especially the parchments.

whatGodIsSaying.headline: A single failure does not define your life; God uses patient mentors to restore broken quitters into indispensable champions of the faith.
whatGodIsSaying.reflection: The argument between Paul and Barnabas in Acts 15 is one of the most painfully honest scenes in the Bible. Both men were spiritual giants, yet they had a 'sharp contention' (*paroxysmos*). Paul was mission-driven: 'Mark quit on us in Pamphylia when the going got tough; soldiers who desert their posts cannot be trusted on the front lines!' Paul wasn't wrong. But Barnabas was people-driven: 'He's a young man who made a mistake; if we discard him now, he'll be ruined forever!' Barnabas wasn't wrong either. They parted company. But notice what God's sovereign grace did with this painful split: instead of one missionary team, there were now two! Paul took Silas through Galatia, and Barnabas took Mark to Cyprus. Barnabas invested unhurried, patient grace into the young quitter. He didn't write Mark off. And what was the fruit of Barnabas' restorative mentoring? Fast forward twenty years: Paul is sitting in a cold, subterranean Roman dungeon awaiting decapitation by Nero. All his fair-weather friends have abandoned him. Demas loved this present world and ran away. Who does Paul ask for on his deathbed? 2 Timothy 4:11: 'Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service!' The man Paul once refused to travel with had become the man Paul could not die without! Furthermore, under the guidance of Peter, this same John Mark penned the Gospel of Mark. God never wastes a failure when grace takes the wheel.

lessons.lesson: Never permanently write someone off because of an early spiritual failure or stumble.
lessons.detail: John Mark deserted the work early in his journey, but with patient mentoring he became an author of Scripture and a hero of the faith.
lessons.question: Is there someone who let you down whom you have written off? Will you give them a second chance?

lessons.lesson: God can multiply His Kingdom impact even through painful interpersonal disagreements.
lessons.detail: The split between Paul and Barnabas was painful, yet God turned it into two missionary journeys that doubled the church's outreach.
lessons.question: Can you trust God's sovereignty to bring good out of a painful relational transition or disagreement?

lessons.lesson: Spiritual maturity admits when a previous evaluation of a person was too harsh.
lessons.detail: Paul had the humility in his final epistle to publicly affirm Mark's usefulness, reconciling and honoring the restored brother.
lessons.question: Do you have the humility to admit when you misjudged someone and celebrate their growth?

lessons.lesson: Invest your time into mentoring and encouraging struggling, younger believers.
lessons.detail: Barnabas' quiet investment in Mark bore eternal fruit; mentoring the next generation is among the highest callings in the Kingdom.
lessons.question: Who is one younger or struggling believer you can take under your wing to encourage this month?

quiz.question: What had John Mark done on the first missionary journey that caused Paul to refuse to take him on the second?
options: He lost all the travel funds
He withdrew from them in Pamphylia and returned home
He refused to preach to Greeks
quiz.explanation: Acts 15:38 notes that Mark 'had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia, and hadn’t gone with them to the work.'

quiz.question: Where did Barnabas take Mark when he separated from Paul in Acts 15:39?
quiz.explanation: Acts 15:39 says: 'Barnabas took Mark with him, and sailed away to Cyprus...'

quiz.question: Whom did Paul choose as his new traveling companion for the second missionary journey?
quiz.explanation: Acts 15:40 records: 'but Paul chose Silas, and went out...'

quiz.question: At the end of his life in 2 Timothy 4:11, Paul ordered that Mark be permanently excommunicated from the church.
quiz.explanation: False. Paul specifically requested: 'Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.'

quiz.question: Who had deserted Paul in 2 Timothy 4:10 because he loved the present world?
quiz.explanation: Paul laments: 'for Demas left me, having loved this present world...'

closingPrayer.guidedPrayer: Lord God of restoration and second chances, I thank You that You do not discard me when I stumble, shrink back, or fail in my duty. Thank You for the tender, patient heart of Barnabas who saw potential in a young deserter and loved him into usefulness. Forgive my harshness toward struggling brothers and sisters who let me down. Give me a restorative spirit that breathes life, hope, and courage into those who have failed. Make me useful for Your service, Lord, and help me to finish my course with unswerving loyalty to Your Kingdom.
closingPrayer.versePrayerLine: “Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.”
closingPrayer.prompt: Pray for someone who recently gave up on their faith or calling: ask God to send a Barnabas to restore them.

310.season: Lystra to Ephesus: The Sincere Faith of a Son in the Gospel
310.theme: Generational faith nurtured quietly in home devotion shapes future leaders for apostolic mission.

memoryVerse.text: having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you; which lived first in your grandmother Lois, and your mother Eunice, and, I am persuaded, in you also.
memoryVerse.whyItMatters: The greatest spiritual legacy is often built not on public stages, but at the kitchen table; godly grandmothers and mothers who saturate children with Scripture shape the champions who advance Christ's global church.

cramData.firstLetters: h b r o t s f t i i y; w l f i y g L, a y m E, a, I a p, i y a.

profile.title: Timothy: The Son in the Faith Formed by Generational Devotion
profile.who: A young disciple from Lystra in Lycaonia, the son of a Greek father and a Jewish-Christian mother named Eunice; nurtured from infancy in the Holy Scriptures by his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice, he possessed an unblemished reputation among local assemblies; recruited by Paul on the second missionary journey, he became Paul's most trusted spiritual son, co-author of several epistles, and bishop of Ephesus.
profile.whenAndWhere: Lystra in southern Galatia, circa AD 50.
profile.family: Mother: Eunice (Jewish believer); Grandmother: Lois; Father: an unnamed Greek.
keyMoments: Growing up in Lystra, being saturated with the Old Testament Scriptures from infancy (2 Timothy 3:15).
Witnessing Paul's stoning and miraculous resurrection during the first missionary journey in Lystra.
Earning a stellar reputation for character and faithfulness among the believers in Lystra and Iconium.
Being selected by Paul as his primary traveling companion and spiritual protege, submitting to circumcision to remove stumbling blocks for Jewish ministry.
Serving as Paul's troubleshooter in troubled churches like Corinth and Philippi, eventually pastoring the church at Ephesus.
profile.strengths: Deeply sincere faith, genuine pastoral care for others ('I have no one like-minded who will sincerely care for your state'), unswerving loyalty.
profile.failures: Struggled with natural timidity, youthfulness, and frequent physical stomach ailments (1 Timothy 4:12, 5:23; 2 Timothy 1:7).

scripture.title: Paul Chooses Timothy as His Protege at Lystra

verses.text: He came to Derbe and Lystra: and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed; but his father was a Greek.
The brothers who were at Lystra and Iconium gave a good testimony about him.
Paul wanted to have him go out with him, and he took and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those parts; for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
